# Armor Class

How Armor Class works in FAND. It replaces the 5e rule where AC is a number an attack must beat. Here, **AC starts at 0, is built up from sources, and then reduces damage.**

## 1. Building AC
Every creature starts at **AC 0**. Add everything below that applies:

| Source | AC gained | Lootable? |
|---|---|---|
| **Constitution** | Con modifier × 2 (never below 0) | No |
| **Natural traits** | Race, subclass, Rune, or monster feature (tough hide, scales, stone skin, etc.). Usually +2 to +10; bosses can go higher | No |
| **Body armor** | Light: level. Medium: level × 1.5. Heavy: level × 2 | Yes (see Looting) |
| **Armor pieces** | Head, Hands, Feet, Shoulders, Back: level ÷ 4 each (minimum 1) | Yes |
| **Shield** | Buckler: level ÷ 3. Shield: level ÷ 2. Tower Shield: level × 0.75 (minimum 1) | Yes |
| **Enhancements** | Runes, coatings, and inserts applied to worn armor: level ÷ 5 (minimum 1) | Only with the armor |
| **Magic** | Spells, potions, and effects such as a Ward Stone's "+1 AC". Temporary unless the item says otherwise | Depends on the item |

All values round down. "Level" is the `level` field on the item's [[FAND/Atrious/Blueprints Index|Blueprint]]. Each armor and shield Blueprint already lists its result in its `ac`, `armorType`, and `slot` fields, and the profession Bases show them as columns.

**Slots:** one Body armor, one Shield, one item per piece slot (Head, Hands, Feet, Shoulders, Back), and one Enhancement per worn armor item. Barding (slot "Mount") is armor for mounts and beasts only: level × 1.5.

**Example:** level 16 heavy plate (32) + level 20 helm (5) + level 13 gauntlets (3) + level 15 tower shield (11) + Con +3 (6) = **AC 57**. That's about 66% reduction.

Dexterity doesn't add to AC. AC now means toughness and protection, not dodging.

**Split AC in two** on every stat block and character sheet:
- **Natural AC**: Constitution + natural traits. It can't be taken.
- **Gear AC**: armor + shield + magic items. It can be looted.

Monsters and bosses should get most of their AC from Natural AC. Then killing them doesn't hand their defense to the party.

## 2. AC as damage reduction (reverse tax brackets)
AC works like tax brackets in reverse. In a tax system, each higher bracket of income is taxed at a *higher* rate. Here, each higher bracket of AC blocks damage at a *lower* rate. Your first 10 AC is worth a lot; your 200th point is worth almost nothing.

The rates follow a 1/x curve, so total reduction climbs toward 100% but **never reaches it**:

> **Reduction % = AC / (AC + 30)**
> **Damage taken = damage × (1 − reduction)**, rounded down, minimum 1.

### Bracket table
Add up the brackets you've filled, the same way you'd work out tax. The "Total reduction" column is that sum at the top of each bracket.

| AC bracket | Each AC point in this bracket blocks | Total reduction at top of bracket | 32-damage hit becomes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0–10 | 2.5% | 25% | 24 |
| 10–20 | 1.5% | 40% | 19 |
| 20–30 | 1.0% | 50% | 16 |
| 30–40 | 0.71% | 57% | 13 |
| 40–50 | 0.54% | 62.5% | 12 |
| 50–60 | 0.42% | 67% | 10 |
| 60–80 | 0.30% | 73% | 8 |
| 80–100 | 0.21% | 77% | 7 |
| 100–150 | 0.13% | 83% | 5 |
| 150–200 | 0.07% | 87% | 4 |
| 200–300 | 0.04% | 91% | 2 |
| 300–500 | 0.017% | 94% | 1 |
| 500+ | keeps shrinking | approaches 100%, never reaches it | 1 (minimum) |

**Example:** AC 35 fills the first three brackets (50%) plus 5 points of the fourth (5 × 0.71% ≈ 3.6%), for about 54% reduction. A 32-damage hit deals 32 × 0.46 = **14**.

### Why brackets
- **Never immune.** Every hit deals at least 1 damage, and the reduction never reaches 100%.
- **No exponential damage race.** Doubling damage always doubles damage taken, whatever the AC.
- **Stacking AC has diminishing returns.** Going from 0 to 30 AC halves damage. Going from 100 to 200 only cuts it from 23% of a hit to 13%. Low AC characters benefit most from their first armor.

## 3. Critical hits (headshots)
A headshot is a critical hit. **Multiply the damage by 1.5, then apply AC** as above.
- 32 damage headshot vs AC 30: 48 × 30/60 = **24**.

*Optional, if crits feel weak:* a headshot also ignores half the target's AC. Using the same example: 48 × 30/45 = **32**.

## 4. Looting armor
Players stripping armor from enemies shouldn't let them skip the AC curve:
1. **Broken on kill.** Armor taken from a creature killed in combat is **Damaged** and gives only half its Gear AC until repaired.
2. **Repair** uses the armor's profession (e.g. [[FAND/Atrious/Professions/Blacksmithing|Blacksmithing]], [[FAND/Atrious/Professions/Tailoring|Tailoring]]). It needs a profession level at least equal to the armor's level, plus one unit of its `materials`, under [[FAND/Atrious/Crafting Rules|Crafting Rules]]. Otherwise it can be sold or broken down for materials by a [[FAND/Atrious/Professions/Scavenging|Scavenging]].
3. **Level requirement.** A character whose level is below the armor's level gets only half its Gear AC.
4. **Natural AC never transfers.** A dragon's scales make a dragon hard to hurt. Its looted scales only matter once someone crafts them into armor.

# Abyss Bestiary

Demons and deep things of the Abyss. From here upward, crafting with these materials needs a Realm Forge (see Custom Blueprints).

Realm: [[Abyss]] (tier 5). A monster's grade is its strength within this realm, from 1 to 10. Its drops use the same scale; see [[FAND/Atrious/Material Grading|Material Grading]] for how grades turn into Item Level. Stripping a corpse for its drops uses the [[FAND/Atrious/Professions/Scavenging|Scavenging]] profession.

## D&D monsters
Official monsters from the Monster Manual (MM), Volo's Guide to Monsters (VGM), Mordenkainen's Tome of Foes (MTF), Fizban's Treasury of Dragons (FTD), and Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants (BGG). Names are official; descriptions are my own and there are no stat blocks, so check the book for stats. CR is from memory; BGG CRs are approximate. Grade comes from CR: CR 0–½ = 1, 1–2 = 2, 3–4 = 3, 5–6 = 4, 7–8 = 5, 9–11 = 6, 12–14 = 7, 15–17 = 8, 18–21 = 9, 22+ = 10. Humanoids drop gear and coin, not materials. **Converting a book stat block to FAND:** keep its HP and damage, and use Natural AC = 2 × (book AC − 10) + CR (see [[FAND/Atrious/Monster Stats|Monster Stats]]). Named unique characters (deities, demon lords, archdevils) are left out; the vault already has renamed versions.

# Inner Realm Bestiary

Guardians and parasites of the Inner Realm, where the Laws are anchored. Killing anything here risks damaging a Law.

Realm: [[Inner Realm]] (tier 6). A monster's grade is its strength within this realm, from 1 to 10. Its drops use the same scale; see [[FAND/Atrious/Material Grading|Material Grading]] for how grades turn into Item Level. Stripping a corpse for its drops uses the [[FAND/Atrious/Professions/Scavenging|Scavenging]] profession.

## D&D monsters
Official monsters from the Monster Manual (MM), Volo's Guide to Monsters (VGM), Mordenkainen's Tome of Foes (MTF), Fizban's Treasury of Dragons (FTD), and Bigby Presents: Glory of the Giants (BGG). Names are official; descriptions are my own and there are no stat blocks, so check the book for stats. CR is from memory; BGG CRs are approximate. Grade comes from CR: CR 0–½ = 1, 1–2 = 2, 3–4 = 3, 5–6 = 4, 7–8 = 5, 9–11 = 6, 12–14 = 7, 15–17 = 8, 18–21 = 9, 22+ = 10. Humanoids drop gear and coin, not materials. **Converting a book stat block to FAND:** keep its HP and damage, and use Natural AC = 2 × (book AC − 10) + CR (see [[FAND/Atrious/Monster Stats|Monster Stats]]). Named unique characters (deities, demon lords, archdevils) are left out; the vault already has renamed versions.

*Artifact — [[FAND/Atrious/Professions/Enchanting|Enchanting]] (Relic Restoration) — Legendary*

88 needles — one per known plane. Finds crossing to any plane from any other.

# Complete Outer Planes Atlas

*Artifact — [[FAND/Atrious/Professions/Navigation|Navigation]] (Astral Navigation) — Rare*

An unusual artifact, built for reading the stars and the space between them using Meridian Glass and Star Chart Fragment. The kind of piece a professional actually reaches for, not just something for a display case.

# Crafting Rules

How a character actually makes something from [[FAND/Atrious/Blueprints Index|Blueprints]], rather than just buying or looting it.

## Requirements

To craft a specific Blueprint item, a character needs all three of the following at once:

1. **The Blueprint itself.** A recipe the character has learned, been taught, or found written down (a physical schematic, a master's notes, a purchased pattern). Knowing a profession does not mean knowing every Blueprint in it — access to the specific recipe is a separate, GM-adjudicated unlock (taught by an NPC, bought from a supplier, found as loot, or reverse-engineered from an existing item — see **Reverse-Engineering** below).
2. **The required Materials.** Every item lists its `materials` field. All of them must be in hand and are consumed on a successful craft (a failed attempt only consumes materials on a natural 1 — see **Crafting Checks**). Materials can come from a market, a [[FAND/Atrious/Professions/Harvesting|Harvesting]] gather or a [[FAND/Atrious/Professions/Scavenging|Scavenging]] harvest from a corpse, or another profession's own byproducts.
3. **The matching Profession, at a high enough level.** The item's `level` field is the minimum profession level required to attempt it at all — a character below that level cannot try, full stop, regardless of materials or blueprint access. This mirrors the level column on every profession's own page (e.g. [[FAND/Atrious/Professions/Blacksmithing|Blacksmithing]]).

If all three are met, the character can attempt the craft. If any one is missing, they can't — no partial credit for having two out of three.

## Crafting Checks

Crafting takes time (see **Time**, below) and ends in one check: **d20 + the profession's crafting bonus** (from that profession's own Level Progression table) **vs. a DC set by the item's rarity**:

| Rarity | DC |
|---|---|
| Common | 10 |
| Uncommon | 13 |
| Rare | 16 |
| Very Rare | 19 |
| Legendary | 22 |
| Artifact | 25 |

- **Success:** the item is completed at the end of the crafting time.
- **Failure:** the attempt fails, but materials aren't lost — the character can try again (spending the time again) once circumstances change, or simply try once more.
- **Natural 1:** the attempt fails *and* the materials are ruined. This is the one case where materials are lost without a completed item.
- **Natural 20:** the item is completed, and the GM may add a minor, non-mechanical flourish (a maker's mark, a slightly finer finish) at no cost.

A character may take a Tertiary-tier item's craft at disadvantage to skip the roll entirely and simply succeed, if the GM judges the item mechanically trivial for that character's profession level (a level-15 Blacksmith doesn't need to sweat a level-1 dagger).

## Time

- **Tertiary-tier items:** roughly a day of dedicated work (or several shorter sessions totaling similar time), assuming a proper workspace.
- **Secondary-tier items:** roughly a week.
- **Primary/Legendary/Artifact-tier items:** at GM discretion, often a month or more, frequently gated behind an in-story requirement beyond just time (a special forge, a particular season, a witness, etc.) on top of the normal three requirements above.

Working without proper tools or a proper workspace for the profession roughly doubles the time and imposes disadvantage on the crafting check.

## Reverse-Engineering

A character with the matching profession, at a level meeting or exceeding the item's own level, who has an example of a finished item in hand for at least one full day, may attempt to learn its Blueprint without ever having been taught it. This requires a crafting check at the same DC as actually making the item (see table above) — success unlocks the Blueprint for future crafting; failure means the item's secrets simply don't give themselves up, though the item itself is undamaged and can be tried again after a long rest.

# Custom Blueprints

Players can design their own unique weapons, armor, and gear instead of relying only on the existing [[FAND/Atrious/Blueprints Index|Blueprints]]. A custom item is built from graded materials (see [[FAND/Atrious/Material Grading|Material Grading]]) and must be made by the right kind of crafter.

Once designed, a custom Blueprint works like any other. It follows the normal [[FAND/Atrious/Crafting Rules|Crafting Rules]], and anyone with the right profession and the Blueprint can make it again.

## Step 1. Concept
Choose:
- **Form**: what the item is (longsword, tower shield, cloak, potion, crossbow, etc.). The form decides the crafter (see Step 3).
- **Name and look**: your own. Keep names original and not taken from other franchises.
- **Purpose**: one sentence on what it's for ("a greatsword that sets the battlefield on fire").

## Step 2. Materials
Every custom item has three kinds of material slot:

| Slot | How many | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| **Primary** | Exactly 1 | Sets the item's **grade**: Item Level, rarity, DC, and damage or AC. |
| **Secondary** | 0–2 | Each adds **one trait** (see Traits). Must be within one realm tier of the primary. |
| **Binding agent** | Required from Hell / Heaven upward | Holds realm materials together. Must be an Essence, Blood, or Crystal material of at least the primary's tier. |

The primary material sets the item's numbers:
- **Material Rank** = (tier − 1) × 10 + grade
- **Item Level** = Rank ÷ 2, rounded up
- **Rarity** follows the table in [[FAND/Atrious/Material Grading|Material Grading]]

## Step 3. Who can craft it
The **form** decides the base profession:

| Form | Crafter |
|---|---|
| Metal weapons, metal armor, helms, gauntlets, metal shields | [[FAND/Atrious/Professions/Blacksmithing\|Blacksmithing]] |
| Bows, staffs, wands, clubs, wooden, stone, bone, dragon-part, and crystal gear | [[FAND/Atrious/Professions/Carving\|Carving]] |
| Cloth and leather armor, cloaks, robes, stealth gear | [[FAND/Atrious/Professions/Tailoring\|Tailoring]] |
| Potions, elixirs, oils, poisons, blood items | [[FAND/Atrious/Professions/Alchemy (Profession)\|Alchemy]] |
| Crossbows, gadgets, constructs, siege weapons, buildings | [[FAND/Atrious/Professions/Engineering\|Engineering]] |
| Runes and sigils on gear; items with a bound soul or elemental core; restored relics | [[FAND/Atrious/Professions/Enchanting\|Enchanting]] |
| Food and drink buffs | [[FAND/Atrious/Professions/Cooking\|Cooking]] |
| Crops, seed stock, livestock lines, mining and foraging tools | [[FAND/Atrious/Professions/Harvesting\|Harvesting]] |
| Corpse-harvesting tools (knives, saws, jars, preservation kits) | [[FAND/Atrious/Professions/Scavenging\|Scavenging]] |
| Maps, charts, navigation instruments | [[FAND/Atrious/Professions/Navigation\|Navigation]] |

**Realm specialties.** Hell, Heaven, and Void metals need a Blacksmith with the matching specialty: Infernal Forging (Hell), Celestial Metallurgy (Heaven), or Void Smithing (Void and Inner Void). Without it, the craft is made at disadvantage. A Blacksmith gains a specialty by finishing one item of that metal under a teacher who has it (see [[FAND/Atrious/Professions/Blacksmithing|Blacksmithing]]).

**Profession level required:**
- Item Level 1–20: profession level at least equal to the Item Level.
- Item Level 21+ (Abyss and above): profession level 20 **and** a **Realm Forge**, a workspace inside or connected to the material's realm. Finding or building one is a story goal the DM sets.

## Step 4. Design check
Writing the Blueprint takes time and one check: **d20 + profession crafting bonus vs the design DC.**

| Primary realm | Design DC | Design time |
|---|---|---|
| Human | 10 (grades 1–5), 13 (6–10) | 1 day |
| Mysterious | 13 (1–5), 16 (6–10) | 2 days |
| Hell / Heaven | 16 (1–5), 19 (6–10) | 1 week |
| Chaos | 19 | 1 week |
| Abyss | 19 (1–5), 22 (6–10) | 2 weeks |
| Inner Realm / Outer Realm | 22 | 1 month |
| Void | 25 | 1 month |
| Inner Void | 27 | 2 months |
| Primordial | 30 | DM's call; always a story event |

- **Success:** the Blueprint exists. Copy the [[FAND/Atrious/Custom Blueprint Template|Custom Blueprint Template]] into `Blueprints/Custom/` and fill it in.
- **Failure:** the design doesn't work yet. You can try again after a long rest. No materials are used, because design happens before crafting.
- **Natural 20:** add one extra trait, even beyond the rarity cap.

Then **craft** the item under [[FAND/Atrious/Crafting Rules|Crafting Rules]], using the same DC. The materials are spent on that craft.

## Step 5. Stats

**Weapons.** Choose the weapon die, then dice = 3 × Item Level ÷ die average, rounded, with a minimum of 1. This is the same formula the existing Blueprints use.

| Weapon size | Die (average) | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| Light | d4 (2.5) | Dagger, dart |
| Simple one-handed | d6 (3.5) | Shortsword, handaxe, shortbow |
| Martial one-handed | d8 (4.5) | Longsword, warhammer, longbow |
| Heavy / polearm | d10 (5.5) | Halberd, glaive, heavy crossbow |
| Great weapon | d12 (6.5) | Greatsword, greataxe, maul |

**Armor and shields.** AC comes from the Item Level, using the tables in [[FAND/Atrious/Armor Class|Armor Class]] (body armor × 1 / 1.5 / 2, pieces ÷ 4, shields ÷ 3 / ÷ 2 / × 0.75).

**Traits come from material properties.** Every material has a **property** listed in the [[FAND/Atrious/Material Index|Material Index]]: a mimic's hide makes an item shapeshift, and an Undead King's Heart turns it into a necromancy focus. The primary material's property always applies, and each secondary material adds its own. Binding agents and supplies add none. See [[FAND/Atrious/Material Properties|Material Properties]] for every property and how it scales with grade. The rarity caps the total:

| Rarity | Max traits |
|---|---|
| Common | 1 |
| Uncommon | 1 |
| Rare | 2 |
| Very Rare | 3 |
| Legendary | 3 |
| Artifact | 4 |

Two materials with the same property don't stack. Use the higher Potency; it still counts as one trait. The DM can swap a property for a fitting custom trait (returning when thrown, a light source, a once-per-day ability) if the design calls for it.

**Realm damage types.** When a property lets you choose a damage type (such as Elemental Core), the primary's realm suggests one:

| Realm | Damage type |
|---|---|
| Human | Weapon's own type |
| Mysterious | Psychic or cold |
| Hell | Fire |
| Heaven | Radiant |
| Chaos | Roll randomly each hit |
| Abyss | Cold or necrotic |
| Inner Realm | Force |
| Outer Realm | Psychic |
| Void | Force |
| Inner Void | Necrotic |
| Primordial | The progenitor's own Law; DM's call |

## Worked example: Cinderfang Greatsword
- **Primary:** Brimstone iron, grade Hell 3. Rank 23 → Item Level 12 → Rare.
- **Secondary:** Imp horn, Hell 3.
- **Binding agent:** Hellhound gland, Hell 2 Blood. It adds no property.
- **Crafter:** Hell metal, so [[FAND/Atrious/Professions/Blacksmithing|Blacksmithing]] level 12 or higher.
- **Design DC:** 16, one week of design time.
- **Damage:** a d12 great weapon, 3 × 12 ÷ 6.5 = 5.54, rounded to **6d12 slashing**.
- **Traits (2 of 2):** Brimstone iron gives **Burning** at Potency 2 (+2d6 fire). The imp horn gives **Piercing Edge** at Potency 2 (ignores 4 AC; crits on 19–20).

## Worked example: Staff of the Dead Court
- **Primary:** Undead King's Heart, grade Mysterious 9. Rank 19 → Item Level 10 → Rare.
- **Secondary:** Shade Heart, Mysterious 6 (from a Shade).
- **Binding agent:** Necromancy Stone, Mysterious 6 (Crystal).
- **Crafter:** a staff with a bound soul, so [[FAND/Atrious/Professions/Enchanting|Enchanting]] level 10 or higher.
- **Design DC:** 16, two days of design time.
- **Traits (2 of 2):** the heart gives **Sovereign of the Dead** at Potency 3 (2, +1 for a grade 9 material): +2 to necromancy spell attacks and DCs, one extra undead per casting, and your undead get +2 to attacks and 15 extra hit points. The shade heart gives **Shadowed** at Potency 1: +1 to Stealth, turn invisible in darkness once per rest, and +1d6 necrotic when the staff strikes.

# Economy

What things cost in FAND: materials, Blueprints, crafting, and services. Prices use the standard coins (1 gp = 10 sp = 100 cp). Every material's price is listed on its note in the [[FAND/Atrious/Materials/Materials.base|Materials database]].

## Material prices
A material's price comes from its realm and grade (see [[FAND/Atrious/Material Grading|Material Grading]]):

> **Price = realm base × grade**, doubled for peak materials (grade 9 and 10).

| Realm | Base (gp) | Grade 1 | Grade 5 | Grade 10 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Human | 5 | 5 | 25 | 100 |
| Mysterious | 50 | 50 | 250 | 1,000 |
| Hell / Heaven | 500 | 500 | 2,500 | 10,000 |
| Chaos | 2,500 | 2,500 | 12,500 | 50,000 |
| Abyss | 10,000 | 10,000 | 50,000 | 200,000 |
| Inner Realm | 50,000 | 50,000 | 250,000 | 1,000,000 |
| Outer Realm | 100,000 | 100,000 | 500,000 | 2,000,000 |
| Void, Inner Void, Primordial | — | not sold | not sold | not sold |

- **Supplies** (oils, inks, wire, tools) cost a fifth of that, minimum 1 gp.
- **Void and above** have no market price. They change hands only between gods, their Fingers, and people desperate enough to trade what gods want.
- Examples: Steel (Human 4) is 20 gp; a Seraph Feather (Heaven 8) is 4,000 gp; Adamantine (Human 10) is 100 gp.

## Buying and selling
| Where | Buys at | Sells at | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ordinary merchant | Half price | Full price | Human materials only; Mysterious in large cities |
| Specialist (a guild or a profession's master) | Half price | Full price | Up to Hell / Heaven materials |
| God's temple | Half price | Full price, minus contract discount | Its own signature materials (see [[FAND/Atrious/God Roster\|God Roster]]); contractors get the rewards in [[FAND/Atrious/God Contracts\|God Contracts]] |
| Black market (Fiend Realm, the Rim of the Abyss) | Three-quarters price | Double price | Hell, Abyss, and Chaos materials; no questions asked, no guarantees |
| Other realms | Their own prices | — | Materials native to a realm cost half there, and foreign materials cost double |

Selling in bulk (more than ten of one material) floods the local market: the price drops by 10% for each further ten sold in the same town that month.

## Blueprints
Buying a Blueprint buys the knowledge, not the item (see [[FAND/Atrious/Crafting Rules|Crafting Rules]]).

| Rarity | Blueprint price |
|---|---|
| Common | 25 gp |
| Uncommon | 100 gp |
| Rare | 500 gp |
| Very Rare | 2,500 gp |
| Legendary | 10,000 gp |
| Artifact | Not for sale; found, earned, or reverse-engineered |

## Finished items and crafting
- **An item's value** is twice the cost of its materials, plus the crafting labor.
- **Labor**, when you hire someone: 10 gp × the item's level per day of crafting time. The crafter's profession level must meet the item's level.
- **Custom Blueprint design** (see [[FAND/Atrious/Custom Blueprints|Custom Blueprints]]): a hired designer charges the Blueprint price for the item's rarity, and the design check still has to succeed.
- **Refining** (see [[FAND/Atrious/Material Refining|Material Refining]]): a hired refiner charges 10% of the result's price.
- **Repairing Damaged armor** (see [[FAND/Atrious/Armor Class|Armor Class]]): one unit of the armor's materials plus a day's labor.

## Services
| Service | Cost |
|---|---|
| Guide to a thin place (Mysterious Realm) | 50 gp |
| Astral Navigator for a crossing | 500 gp per day |
| Passage through a guarded gate (Hell / Heaven) | 1,000 gp bribe, or a favor |
| Realm Forge rental | 1% of the item's value per day |
| Realm-sealed storage for foreign materials | 5 gp per material per month |
| Gathering rights on claimed land | 10% of what you gather |

## Contract tithes
Gods expect a share from their contractors (see [[FAND/Atrious/God Contracts|God Contracts]]):
- **Minor and Normal:** a tenth of income from work done in the god's name.
- **Major and Senior:** a tenth, plus the god's tasks.
- **Apostle and above:** no tithe. The god provides; the contractor provides the god.

# God Contracts

A **contract** is a formal agreement between a mortal and a [[God]]. The god lends a share of its power. In return, the mortal spreads the god's Law, does its work, and fights its wars.

Gods need contracts. Every god is a replica powered by Runes. It only grows stronger by stealing power from other gods or by getting more mortals to follow its Law (see [[Runes]]). Contractors are how a god reaches into the mortal world to do both.

Contracts are different from two existing mechanics:
- **[[Pacts]]** are loans from devils, paid back later.
- **[[Worship]]** is devotion without terms.

A contract is a **rank in a god's service**, with clear duties and a clear reward.

## The ten ranks (weakest to strongest)

| # | Rank | Holders per god | Power granted | Natural AC | Can grant contracts up to |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Minor** | Unlimited | One cantrip from the god's Law; +1 to one skill tied to the god | +1 | — |
| 2 | **Normal** | Unlimited | One 1st-level spell of the god's Law, once per long rest; the god can send you dreams | +2 | — |
| 3 | **Major** | Hundreds | The god's spells up to 2nd level; you can sense other contractors of your god | +3 | — |
| 4 | **Senior** | Dozens | Spells up to 3rd level; resistance to one damage type tied to the god | +4 | Minor |
| 5 | **Apostle** | 12 | Spells up to 5th level; a **Secondary-tier** link to the god's Rune, which unlocks one unique ability (see [[Class]]) | +6 | Normal |
| 6 | **5th Finger** | 1 | Spells up to 6th level; a **Primary-tier** fragment of the god's Rune, with its own unique ability | +8 | Major |
| 7 | **4th Finger** | 1 | Spells up to 7th level; immune to being charmed or frightened by other gods' contractors | +10 | Senior |
| 8 | **3rd Finger** | 1 | Spells up to 8th level; once per day, use one of the god's Rune spells without holding the Rune | +12 | Senior |
| 9 | **2nd Finger** | 1 | Spells up to 9th level; can **create new spells** from the god's Law, which normally only those close to godhood can do | +14 | Apostle |
| 10 | **1st Finger** | 1 | Acts as the god's avatar: speaks with its voice and can channel its power directly; everything above | +16 | Apostle |

### How the table works
- **Spells.** Contract spells are extra spells from the god's Law. You can cast them even if your class can't. They use your class's spell slots, or once per long rest each if you have no slots.
- **Natural AC.** The god's power toughens the contractor. This counts as **Natural AC** under [[FAND/Atrious/Armor Class|Armor Class]], so it can't be looted. It replaces the previous rank's bonus rather than stacking with it.
- **The Hand.** Every god has exactly **five Fingers**, from the 5th Finger up to the 1st. Together they're called the god's **Hand**. Each position has one holder at a time. A god's Hand is the most dangerous group of mortals it controls.
- **Granting contracts.** From Senior upward, a contractor can sign lower-rank contracts on the god's behalf. That's how a god's reach spreads through a region.

## Duties
Every contract has duties. They grow with the rank:

| Ranks | Duties |
|---|---|
| Minor, Normal | Obey the god's core rule (its Law); a small task or offering now and then |
| Major, Senior | Spread worship (bring new followers); take missions from the god's higher contractors |
| Apostle | Lead a region or order for the god; answer any summons |
| Fingers | Act as the god's weapon in wars with other gods; guard the god's Runes; carry out the god's bets on mortal wars and successions |

Each god's specific wants are listed in the [[FAND/Atrious/God Roster|God Roster]].

## Rewards
Besides spells and Natural AC, gods pay in **materials** and **craft**. Every god in the [[FAND/Atrious/God Roster|God Roster]] has three signature materials (Normal, Senior, and Apostle) and a unique Finger relic.

| Rank | Reward |
|---|---|
| Minor | Buy Human-grade materials at the god's temples at a discount |
| Normal | The god's temples sell its **Normal signature material** to you |
| Major | One free **Normal signature material** per completed task; temple crafters work for you at half cost |
| Senior | One **Senior signature material** each time you rise in rank or finish a major task; access to one existing Blueprint that fits the god's theme |
| Apostle | One **Apostle signature material** on taking the seat; the god's home realm counts as a Realm Forge for you (see [[FAND/Atrious/Custom Blueprints\|Custom Blueprints]]) |
| 5th–2nd Finger | A personal relic of your own design, crafted by the god's forges from its Apostle signature material; Potency counts as 2 higher than normal |
| 1st Finger | The god's **Finger relic** itself |

Signature materials are what the god gives freely. Contractors can still gather or buy any other material.

## Rising in rank
To rise, a contractor must **complete a task the god sets** and meet the rank's requirement:

| Moving to | Requirement |
|---|---|
| Normal, Major | Serve faithfully and finish the god's tasks |
| Senior | Bring the god a meaningful number of new followers, or win a notable victory in its name |
| Apostle | An Apostle seat must be empty (by death, betrayal, or promotion), and the god must choose you |
| Any Finger | The position must be empty, **or you defeat its current holder** |

Gods allow Fingers to be taken by force. A Finger who can be killed wasn't strong enough to hold the position.

## One god at a time
- **Minor and Normal** contracts can be held with several gods at once, like hired work.
- **Major and above** are exclusive: one god only. Taking a second contract at Major or higher breaks the first (see below).
- Contractors of rival gods are fair game for each other. The higher your rank, the more other gods' contractors will want you dead.

## Breaking a contract

| Rank | What happens |
|---|---|
| Minor, Normal | All contract power is lost immediately |
| Major, Senior | Power is lost, and the god places a curse: a DM-chosen disadvantage until you atone or the god dies |
| Apostle | Power and Natural AC are lost, and the god sends its other contractors to hunt you |
| Fingers | The Rune fragment tears itself out. Make a Constitution save (DC 10 + 2 × rank number). On a failure you drop to 0 hit points. The god's whole Hand hunts you |

## When a god dies
Gods are killed and usurped all the time. When a god dies:
- All its contracts become void. Contractors lose contract power at the start of their next long rest.
- The god's power breaks into **Runes**, as every dead god's does.
- Its Fingers are closest to that power. A Finger who reaches the god's remains first may claim a Primary piece (see [[Class]]) before rivals or the killer take it. This is how a 1st Finger can take the first step toward becoming a god.

# God Roster

Every god that offers [[FAND/Atrious/God Contracts|contracts]] in FAND. Each is a replica built from the Runes of a dead original god (see [[Runes]]). A god's power is the Runes it holds, so **gods that hold the same Rune are rivals**: each wants the other's share. Only [[Infinatas]] is still an original.

The pantheons are drawn from real-world mythology (see the [[FAND/Atrious/Gods Index|Gods Index]]). In FAND they are the current holders of those names and Runes, not necessarily the gods from the myths.

## How to read an entry
- **Runes:** the Laws the god holds. Its contractors' spells come from these.
- **Home realm:** where its temple-palace stands. Its Apostles can use that realm as a Realm Forge.
- **Wants:** the duties it gives contractors.
- **Signature materials:** what it rewards contractors with at Normal, Senior, and Apostle rank (see Rewards in [[FAND/Atrious/God Contracts|God Contracts]]).
- **Finger relic:** the unique item carried by its 1st Finger.
- **The Hand:** how many of its five Finger seats are filled. Empty seats can be claimed.
- **Rivals:** gods that share one of its Runes.

# Aztec Pantheon

## Quetzalcoatl - The Feathered Serpent
The feathered serpent god of wind, learning, and civilization, one of the central deities of Mesoamerican mythology.

## Tlaloc - God of Rain
God of rain, fertility, and water, both a giver of life-sustaining rain and a bringer of storms and drought.

## Xipe Totec - God of Renewal
God of spring, agriculture, and renewal, whose myths involve shedding an old skin for a new one.

## Chalchiuhtlicue - Goddess of Water
Goddess of lakes, rivers, and running water, consort of Tlaloc.

## Tonatiuh - God of the Warrior Spirit
The sun god who demanded sacrifice to keep the sun moving across the sky, and patron of warriors.

# Celtic Pantheon

## Morrigan - Goddess of Fate
Goddess of war, fate, and death, often appearing as a crow over battlefields to claim the fallen.

## Cernunnos - God of Wild Things
Horned god of wild animals, the forest, and fertility.

## Brigid - Goddess of Healing
Goddess of healing, poetry, and smithcraft, later syncretized into the Christian Saint Brigid.

## Dagda - Father of the Celtic Gods
Father-figure of the Tuatha Dé Danann, god of abundance, wisdom, and druidry, owner of a cauldron that never runs empty.

## Lugh - God of Craftsmanship
God of skill and craftsmanship, master of every trade at once, associated with the harvest festival Lughnasadh.

# Egyptian Pantheon

## Ra - God of the Sun
Sun god and king of the gods, who sails across the sky by day and through the underworld by night.

## Osiris - God of Rebirth
God of the afterlife and resurrection, murdered and dismembered by his brother Set before being restored to rule the underworld.

## Isis - Goddess of Magic
Goddess of magic and motherhood, who reassembled Osiris's body and protected their son Horus.

## Horus - God of the Sky
Falcon-headed sky god, avenger of his father Osiris and patron of kingship.

## Thoth - God of Knowledge
Ibis-headed god of writing, knowledge, and the moon, credited with inventing language.

## Bastet - Goddess of Protection
Cat goddess of protection, home, and fertility.

## Hathor - Goddess of Music
Goddess of music, love, and joy, often depicted as a cow or a woman with cow's horns cradling the sun.

## Sobek - God of the Nile
Crocodile-headed god of the Nile, associated with strength, fertility, and military prowess.

## Khnum - God of Creation
Ram-headed god said to have shaped humankind from clay on a potter's wheel.

## Neith - Goddess of Weaving
Goddess of weaving, hunting, and war, sometimes credited as a creator deity who wove the world into being.

# Greek Pantheon

## Zeus - King of the Olympian Gods
Ruler of Olympus and god of sky and thunder, who overthrew his father Cronus to lead the second generation of gods.

## Hera - Queen of the Gods
Zeus's wife and queen of Olympus, goddess of marriage and family, often defined in myth by her jealousy of Zeus's affairs.

## Poseidon - God of the Sea
Brother of Zeus and god of the sea, earthquakes, and horses, quick to anger and slow to forgive a slight.

## Demeter - Goddess of the Harvest
Goddess of agriculture and the harvest, whose grief over her daughter Persephone's abduction is said to have created the seasons.

## Athena - Goddess of Wisdom
Goddess of wisdom and strategic warfare, born fully armored from Zeus's head.

## Apollo - God of Prophecy and Music
God of the sun, music, prophecy, and healing, twin brother of Artemis.

## Artemis - Goddess of the Hunt
Goddess of the hunt, wilderness, and the moon, fiercely protective of her independence.

## Aphrodite - Goddess of Love and Beauty
Goddess of love, beauty, and desire, born from sea foam.

## Hephaestus - God of the Forge
God of fire, blacksmiths, and craftsmen, the only Olympian associated with a physical disability, honored for his skill regardless.

## Hermes - Messenger of the Gods
Messenger god of travelers, trade, and thieves, known for speed and cunning.

## Dionysus - God of Wine and Revelry
God of wine, festivity, and religious ecstasy, capable of both joyous celebration and destructive madness.

## Persephone - Queen of Spring
Demeter's daughter, abducted by Hades to become queen of the underworld, splitting her year between the two realms and bringing spring when she returns.

## Hecate - Goddess of Magic
Goddess of magic, witchcraft, and crossroads, associated with the night and the moon.

## Nyx - Goddess of Night
Primordial goddess of night, powerful enough that even Zeus is said to fear her.

## Hypnos - God of Sleep
God of sleep, twin brother of Thanatos (death), living in a cave where the sun never reaches.

## Nemesis - Goddess of Balance
Goddess of retribution, who brings down those who succumb to hubris or take more than their share of fortune.

## Eos - Goddess of the Dawn
Goddess of the dawn, who rises each morning from the edge of the world to announce the sun's arrival.

## Selene - Goddess of the Moon
Goddess who personifies the moon itself, driving her chariot across the night sky.

## Helios - God of the Sun
God who personifies the sun, driving a chariot of fire across the sky from east to west each day.

## Tyche - Goddess of Fortune
Goddess of luck and fortune, whose favor determines the rise and fall of cities as much as individuals.

# Hindu Pantheon

## Brahma - The Creator God
The creator god of the Hindu trimurti, who brought the universe into being at the start of each cosmic cycle.

## Vishnu - The Preserver
The preserver god of the trimurti, who maintains cosmic order and descends to earth in avatars whenever balance is threatened.

## Shiva - The Transformer
The transformer and destroyer god of the trimurti, whose destruction clears the way for renewal.

## Ganesha - God of Beginnings
Elephant-headed god of new beginnings, wisdom, and the remover of obstacles.

## Lakshmi - Goddess of Fortune
Goddess of wealth, fortune, and prosperity, consort of Vishnu.

## Saraswati - Goddess of the Arts
Goddess of knowledge, music, and the arts, consort of Brahma.

## Indra - God of Thunder
King of the Devas and god of thunder, storms, and war.

## Varuna - God of Cosmic Order
God of the sky, oceans, and cosmic law, keeper of rita, the order underlying the universe.

## Surya - God of the Sun
The sun god, who rides a chariot pulled across the sky by seven horses.

## Parvati - Goddess of Devotion
Goddess of love, devotion, and fertility, consort of Shiva and mother of Ganesha.

# Japanese Pantheon

## Amaterasu - Goddess of the Sun
The sun goddess and most revered deity in Shinto, said to be the ancestor of the Japanese imperial line.

## Susanoo - God of Storms
God of storms and the sea, Amaterasu's brother, known for both destructive rages and heroic deeds.

## Tsukuyomi - God of the Moon
God of the moon, brother of Amaterasu, whose falling-out with her is said to explain why day and night are separate.

## Izanagi - God of Creation
Primordial god who, with his sister-wife Izanami, created the islands of Japan and the first gods.

## Inari - God of Prosperity
Deity of rice, fertility, and prosperity, often depicted with fox messengers called kitsune.

# Mesopotamian Pantheon

## Enki - God of Wisdom
God of wisdom, water, and creation in Sumerian mythology, patron of crafts and civilization.

## Enlil - God of the Wind
God of wind, air, and storms, and chief of the Sumerian pantheon for much of its history.

## Inanna - Goddess of Love
Goddess of love, beauty, and war, whose descent into the underworld is one of the oldest recorded myths.

## Anu - God of the Sky
The sky god and, in the earliest Sumerian tradition, the supreme deity from whom other gods derived their authority.

## Utu - God of Justice
Sun god and god of justice, who judges the living and the dead by the light he casts on all things.

# Norse Pantheon

## Odin - Allfather of the Norse Gods
Allfather of the Aesir, god of wisdom, war, and death, who traded an eye for knowledge at Mimir's well.

## Thor - God of Thunder
God of thunder and protector of Asgard, wielder of the hammer Mjolnir.

## Freya - Goddess of Love
Goddess of love, fertility, and war, who claims half the warriors who die in battle for her own hall.

## Tyr - God of Justice
God of law and heroic glory, who sacrificed his hand to bind the wolf Fenrir.

## Baldur - God of Light
The most beloved of the Aesir, god of light and purity, whose death was engineered by Loki.

## Mimir - God of Wisdom
A being renowned for wisdom, whose severed head Odin kept and consulted for counsel.

## Skadi - Goddess of Winter
Giantess and goddess of winter, skiing, and the hunt, who married into the Aesir after a failed vengeance quest.

## Njord - God of the Sea
God of the sea, seafaring, and wealth, father of Freyr and Freya.

## Idun - Goddess of Youth
Keeper of the golden apples that keep the Aesir eternally young.

## Forseti - God of Reconciliation
God of justice and reconciliation, said to settle disputes so fairly that all parties leave satisfied.

# Material Grading

Every crafting material in FAND has a **grade**: the **realm** it comes from, then a **number from 1 to 10** for how strong it is within that realm. Examples: `Human 4`, `Hell 7`, `Abyss 10`.

Materials include both **ores** (metal, stone, crystal, wood) and **monster materials** (hide, bone, scale, blood, organs, essences). A Hell 3 ore and a Hell 3 monster fang have the same grade and power. What differs is what they're good for (see Material Types).

Grades drive [[FAND/Atrious/Custom Blueprints|Custom Blueprints]]: the grade of an item's primary material sets its level, rarity, and crafting DC.

## Realm ranking (weakest to strongest)

| Tier | Realm | What it is | Material Rank | Item Level | Rarity |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Human** | The [[Mortal Realm]]: ordinary ores, beasts, and plants | 1–10 | 1–5 | Common (1–5), Uncommon (6–10) |
| 2 | **[[Mysterious Realm\|Mysterious]]** | The in-between places: the [[Astral]], the [[Mirror Realm]], fey pockets, and the edges of the [[Spirit Realm]] | 11–20 | 6–10 | Uncommon (1–5), Rare (6–10) |
| 3 | **Hell / Heaven** | [[Hell]] (including the [[Fiend Realm]]) and [[Heaven]]. Same tier, opposite natures | 21–30 | 11–15 | Rare (1–5), Very Rare (6–10) |
| 4 | **[[Chaos Realm\|Chaos]]** | Places where [[Chaos]] has broken reality into constant change | 31–40 | 16–20 | Very Rare |
| 5 | **[[Abyss]]** | The bottomless dark below Hell, where what falls never lands | 41–50 | 21–25 | Very Rare (1–5), Legendary (6–10) |
| 6 | **[[Inner Realm]]** | The core layers every realm rests on, where the Laws are anchored | 51–60 | 26–30 | Legendary |
| 7 | **Outer Realm** | The [[Outer Realm]], past the Astral, where no god has confirmed what's there | 61–70 | 31–35 | Legendary |
| 8 | **Void** | The [[Void]], where Spin, Time, Gravity, and Balance were pulled from. Nothing has ever lived there | 71–80 | 36–40 | Artifact |
| 9 | **Inner Void** | The [[Inner Void]], the deepest Void, near the source of Emptiness and Zero | 81–90 | 41–45 | Artifact |
| 10 | **[[Primordial Realm\|Primordial]]** | Remains of the original gods and dead progenitors, found only in the depths of the [[Spirit Realm]] or on the corpse of a god | 91–100 | 46–50 | Artifact |

Tiers 8–10 (Void, Inner Void, Primordial) are new additions to finish your list above Outer Realm.

**Material Rank** = (tier − 1) × 10 + grade. Hell 7 = 20 + 7 = **Rank 27**.
**Item Level** = Material Rank ÷ 2, rounded up. Hell 7 → **Level 14**.

Item Levels 1–20 cover the same range as the existing [[FAND/Atrious/Blueprints Index|Blueprints]], from Human through Chaos. Anything from the Abyss upward goes beyond mortal gear.

## Grade 1–10 within a realm

| Grade | Meaning | Typical source |
|---|---|---|
| 1–3 | Common for that realm | Surface ore veins, weak local creatures |
| 4–6 | Uncommon | Deep veins, average monsters, elites |
| 7–9 | Rare | Named monsters, guarded deposits, rare plants |
| 10 | Unique | A realm's boss, a one-of-a-kind deposit, a god's leftovers |

**Grading monster materials:** grade the creature by how strong it is *for its realm*. A hellhound is a common Hell beast (Hell 2–3). A Hell general is Hell 9. The same creature always gives the same grade, but a DM can raise a grade by 1 for an exceptional specimen.

## Material types
The type decides which profession works a material and what traits it can add.

| Type | Examples | Usually worked by | Typical traits |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Ore / Metal** | Iron, silver, brimstone iron, nullsteel | [[FAND/Atrious/Professions/Blacksmithing\|Blacksmithing]] | Damage, AC, durability |
| **Wood / Plant** | Oak, wisp-willow, ash of a burnt god-tree | [[FAND/Atrious/Professions/Carving\|Carving]], [[FAND/Atrious/Professions/Alchemy (Profession)\|Alchemy]] | Reach, range, spell focus |
| **Crystal / Gem** | Quartz, mirror shard, zero-glass | [[FAND/Atrious/Professions/Carving\|Carving]] | Spell power, stored charges |
| **Stone** | Granite, anchorstone | [[FAND/Atrious/Professions/Carving\|Carving]] | AC, weight, shields |
| **Hide / Cloth / Fiber** | Wolf pelt, fey silk, shadow thread | [[FAND/Atrious/Professions/Tailoring\|Tailoring]] | Light armor, stealth, resistances |

# Material Index

Every graded material in FAND: 1597 in total. 359 come from the existing Blueprints and 1238 are new, from the Bestiary and Gathering pages. Rules: [[FAND/Atrious/Material Grading|Material Grading]].

**Notes on grading the existing materials**
- A Blueprint's `level` is the profession skill needed to make it; a material's grade is the material's own power. They don't have to match. Every Blueprint now also lists `materialGrade` and `materialRank` for its strongest material.
- Void-named materials in the existing Blueprints (Voidmetal, Void Nullstone, etc.) are Void leakage caught in lower realms, graded Mysterious or Chaos. True Void materials, such as Nullsteel, start at Void 1.
- Every material has a **property** it gives to a [[FAND/Atrious/Custom Blueprints|Custom Blueprint]]. How properties work and scale: [[FAND/Atrious/Material Properties|Material Properties]].
- Supplies (oils, inks, wire, tools) are graded low and can't be used as a Primary or Secondary material.

# Material Properties

Every material has a **property**: what it adds to an item when used in a [[FAND/Atrious/Custom Blueprints|Custom Blueprint]]. A mimic's hide lets a weapon change shape. An Undead King's Heart makes an item a necromancy focus that strengthens your undead. Each material's property is listed in the [[FAND/Atrious/Material Index|Material Index]] and on its Bestiary or Gathering page.

## How properties work
- The **primary** material's property always applies. Each **secondary** material adds its property. Binding agents and supplies add none.
- The item's rarity caps how many properties it can hold (see Custom Blueprints).
- The same property twice doesn't stack: use the higher Potency.
- **Existing Blueprints:** every weapon, armor, and shield Blueprint carries the property of its strongest non-supply material, on top of its written stats. It's listed in the note's `property` and `potency` fields, in a Material Property section, and as columns in each profession's Base. Other categories (artifacts, potions, and so on) keep only their written stats.

## Potency
A property's strength comes from the material's grade:

- **Potency** = Item Level ÷ 5, rounded down (minimum 1).
- **Peak materials** are stronger: grade 9 adds +1 Potency and grade 10 adds +2 (maximum 10). A realm's best materials outclass the next realm's weakest.
- **B** (the bonus) = Potency ÷ 2, rounded up, so 1 to 5.
- Save DCs from properties are **10 + 2×B**.

| Realm | Potency range |
|---|---|
| Human | 1–3 |
| Mysterious | 1–4 |
| Hell / Heaven | 2–5 |
| Chaos | 3–6 |
| Abyss | 4–7 |
| Inner Realm | 5–8 |
| Outer Realm | 6–9 |
| Void | 7–10 |
| Inner Void | 8–10 |
| Primordial | 9–10 |

## How a material gets its property
Named materials use the property that fits them best:
- Mimic, doppelganger, and lycanthrope parts → **Shapeshifting**
- Lich, vampire, death knight, mummy lord, and Undead King parts → **Sovereign of the Dead**
- Other undead parts → **Necromantic**
- Beholder kin → **Eye Ray**. Mind flayer kin → **Mind Blast**. Phoenix → **Rebirth**. Tarrasque and behemoth → **Invulnerable**
- Progenitor remains (Ignis Cinder, Undine Tear, Sylph Breath, Gnome Knuckle) → **Progenitor Piece**. Remains of original gods → **Divine Spark**
- Element words (fire, frost, storm, acid, venom, holy, shadow, psychic, and so on) → the matching elemental property. Dragon parts follow the dragon's color.

Anything else falls back on its realm, then on its type:

| Realm fallback (hides, bones, blood, essences) | Property |
|---|---|
| Hell, Abyss | Dreadful |
| Heaven | Holy |
| Chaos | Chaotic |
| Inner Realm | Lawful |
| Outer Realm | Farreaching |
| Void, Inner Void | Nullifying |
| Primordial | Divine Spark |

| Type fallback | Property |
|---|---|
| Ore / Metal | Tempered |
| Wood / Plant | Living |
| Crystal / Gem | Spell Vessel |
| Stone | Enduring |
| Hide / Cloth / Fiber | Supple |
| Bone / Fang / Horn / Scale | Piercing Edge |
| Blood / Organ | Lifedrinking |
| Essence / Soul / Core | Elemental Core |
| Mechanism | Mechanical |
| Supply | none |

The DM can overrule any assignment that doesn't fit.

# Material Refining

Refining combines several lower-grade materials into one of a higher grade, so low-level loot keeps its value as the party grows. Grades are explained in [[FAND/Atrious/Material Grading|Material Grading]].

## Within a realm
Combine **3 materials of the same type and grade** (for example, three Human 4 Ore / Metal) into **1 material one grade higher** (Human 5) of the same realm and type.

- **Who can refine:** the profession that works that material type (see Material Types in Material Grading). [[FAND/Atrious/Professions/Scavenging|Scavengers]] can refine organic types (hide, bone, blood, essence), at disadvantage.
- **Check:** d20 + profession crafting bonus vs the design DC for the *result's* grade (see the table in [[FAND/Atrious/Custom Blueprints|Custom Blueprints]]).
- **Time:** 1 day per grade of the result.
- **Failure:** one input is lost. A natural 1 ruins them all.

## Crossing into the next realm
Grade 10 of a realm can be refined into grade 1 of the next realm up, but it's harder:

- **5 materials** of grade 10 and the same type, not 3;
- a **binding agent** from the destination realm (any Essence, Blood, or Crystal of that realm);
- a **Realm Forge** of the destination realm, or the home realm of a god whose contract you hold at Apostle rank or higher;
- the check is at disadvantage.

For example, five Human 10 Adamantine plus a Mysterious binding agent could become one Mysterious 1 metal.

## Limits
- **Primordial** materials can't be made by refining. They're only found.
- **Supplies** can't be refined.
- Inputs must share a **type**. Mixed types can't be combined.
- The result's **name and property** are the refiner's choice from among the inputs. A refined material is a new named material; give it a name and write it into the [[FAND/Atrious/Material Index|Material Index]] and the materials database if you want to reuse it.

## Why bother
| From | To | Materials needed |
|---|---|---|
| Human 1 | Human 5 | 81 |
| Human 7 | Human 10 | 27 |
| Human 10 | Mysterious 1 | 5 plus a binding agent |

Refining is cheaper than it looks for mid-grade materials and punishing for low ones. Past the first two realms, it's usually faster to travel and gather (see [[FAND/Atrious/Realm Travel|Realm Travel]]).

# Monster Stats

How monsters work with FAND's rules, where [[FAND/Atrious/Armor Class|Armor Class]] reduces damage instead of being a number to beat.

## Homebrew monsters
Every original monster in the Bestiaries has stats built from its realm and grade (see [[FAND/Atrious/Material Grading|Material Grading]]):

| Stat | Formula |
|---|---|
| **Level** | Item Level of its grade: Material Rank ÷ 2, rounded up |
| **HP** | 12 × Level (doubled for grade 10 bosses) |
| **Natural AC** | 2 × Level |
| **Attacks** | 1 below Level 5, 2 from Level 5, 3 from Level 15 |
| **Damage per attack** | 3 × Level ÷ attacks ÷ 4.5, rounded, in d8s (minimum 1d8) |
| **Save DC** | 10 + Level ÷ 3, rounded up |
| **Trait** | The [[FAND/Atrious/Material Properties\|property]] of its strongest drop, at that drop's Potency, applied to the monster itself |
| **Boss (grade 10)** | Double HP and 3 legendary actions per round (one attack each) |

A monster's damage matches a weapon of the same Item Level (see [[FAND/Atrious/Custom Blueprints|Custom Blueprints]]), so a fight between a monster and gear of its own grade is even.

| Example | Level | HP | Natural AC | Attacks |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Marsh Troll (Human 6) | 3 | 36 | 6 (17%) | 1 × 2d8 |
| Behemoth (Human 10, boss) | 5 | 120 | 10 (25%) | 2 × 2d8 |
| Seraph (Heaven 8) | 14 | 168 | 28 (48%) | 2 × 5d8 |
| The Unclaimed (Void 10, boss) | 40 | 960 | 80 (73%) | 3 × 9d8 |

## Official D&D monsters
Official monsters keep their book stat blocks (hit points, attacks, damage, abilities). Only AC changes:

> **FAND Natural AC = 2 × (book AC − 10) + CR** (minimum 0)

| Example | Book AC | CR | FAND Natural AC | Damage reduction |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Goblin | 15 | ¼ | 10 | 25% |
| Owlbear | 13 | 3 | 9 | 23% |
| Adult Red Dragon | 19 | 17 | 35 | 54% |
| Tarrasque | 25 | 30 | 60 | 67% |

Their grade (from CR) and drops are listed in each realm's Bestiary.

## Attacking
Attacks still roll to hit as your table normally does. What changes is what armor does after a hit: the damage is reduced by the target's AC brackets. Monster traits and material properties apply after the roll.

# Player's Guide

A plain-language tour of what makes FAND different from standard D&D. It covers the rules you'll use at the table, and each section links to the full rules page.

## 1. The world in one paragraph
The gods of FAND are copies. The original gods died, and their power broke apart into **Runes**, the Laws of the world (Fire, Time, Love, Death...). Today's gods are built from stolen Runes, and they grow stronger by stealing more or by getting mortals to follow their Law. That's why gods want you. See [[Runes]] and the [[FAND/Atrious/God Roster|God Roster]].

## 2. Your class and Runes
Your class works like normal D&D 5e. If your class is tied to a Rune, owning a piece of the dead god or spirit behind that Rune makes you stronger:
- **Tertiary:** anything themed on the Rune. Raises power only.
- **Secondary:** a relic once removed from the source. Unlocks a unique ability.
- **Primary:** a piece of the source itself. Unlocks a stronger unique ability.

See [[Class]].

## 3. Armor Class works differently
- Your AC **starts at 0**. It comes from Constitution, natural traits, armor, shields, and magic.
- AC doesn't make attacks miss. It **reduces damage** after a hit: AC 10 blocks 25%, AC 30 blocks half, and AC 90 blocks three quarters. It never reaches 100%, and every hit does at least 1 damage.
- Headshots are critical hits: ×1.5 damage before AC.
- Armor looted from enemies is Damaged (half AC) until it's repaired.

See [[FAND/Atrious/Armor Class|Armor Class]].

## 4. Materials have grades
Every material comes from a **realm** and has a **grade from 1 to 10** in it, like `Hell 7`. Realms rank from weakest to strongest: Human, Mysterious, Hell/Heaven, Chaos, Abyss, Inner Realm, Outer Realm, Void, Inner Void, Primordial. Better realm and grade means stronger gear. Every material also has a **property**: fire materials burn, mimic parts shapeshift, undead remains make necromancy foci.

See [[FAND/Atrious/Material Grading|Material Grading]], [[FAND/Atrious/Material Properties|Material Properties]], and the [[FAND/Atrious/Materials/Materials.base|Materials database]].

## 5. Getting materials
- **Hunt and scavenge:** monsters carry materials of their realm and grade. Stripping a corpse for hide, bone, blood, organs, and essences uses the **Scavenging** profession. See the Bestiaries in the [[FAND/Atrious/Material Index|Material Index]].
- **Harvest:** ore, stone, crystals, and plants are gathered with the **Harvesting** profession, listed on each realm's Gathering page.
- **Buy:** prices depend on grade (Steel is 20 gp, a Seraph Feather 4,000 gp). See [[FAND/Atrious/Economy|Economy]].
- **Refine:** three of one grade make one of the next grade. See [[FAND/Atrious/Material Refining|Material Refining]].

## 6. Professions and crafting
There are **10 professions**:

| Profession | Makes or does |
|---|---|
| Blacksmithing | Metal weapons and armor |
| Carving | Wood, stone, bone, and crystal gear |
| Tailoring | Cloth and leather gear |
| Alchemy | Potions and poisons |
| Cooking | Meals that buff |
| Enchanting | Runes, glyphs, and bound souls |
| Engineering | Machines, constructs, and buildings |
| Harvesting | Gathers ore and plants, raises animals |
| Scavenging | Strips corpses for parts |
| Navigation | Maps and instruments |

Each has **specialties**. You start with one and gain more as you level; crafting outside them is at disadvantage. See the [[FAND/Atrious/Profession Quick Reference|Profession Quick Reference]] and [[FAND/Atrious/Master Professions|Master Professions]].

You can also design your own unique items:
1. Pick a form (sword, cloak, potion...). The form decides which profession makes it.
2. Pick a **primary** material (sets its power) and up to two **secondary** materials (each adds its property).
3. Make a design check, then craft it.

Your profession level goes up as you craft. See [[FAND/Atrious/Custom Blueprints|Custom Blueprints]], [[FAND/Atrious/Crafting Rules|Crafting Rules]], and [[FAND/Atrious/Profession Progression|Profession Progression]].

## 7. Contracts with gods
A god can offer you a **contract**: its power in exchange for your service. Ranks run from Minor up to Apostle, then the five **Fingers**, the god's personal Hand. Higher ranks give spells, Natural AC, and rare materials, but come with duties, rivals, and a price for breaking faith. Gods who hold the same Rune are enemies, and so are their contractors.

See [[FAND/Atrious/God Contracts|God Contracts]] and the [[FAND/Atrious/God Roster|God Roster]].

## 8. Travelling between realms
Other realms push back on visitors. Each realm has a **Pressure** (Mysterious 1, Hell 2... Primordial 9). Your **Attunement** comes from your level, your contract rank, or gear made from that realm's materials. If Pressure is higher, you suffer strain (disadvantage, then exhaustion). Getting there takes thin places, the Astral, gates, rifts, or a god's invitation.

See [[FAND/Atrious/Realm Travel|Realm Travel]] and the [[FAND/Atrious/Realm Map|Realm Map]].

## Quick reference
| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| How much damage does my armor stop? | AC ÷ (AC + 30) |
| How strong is a material? | Realm tier and grade → Material Rank → Item Level |
| How strong is its property? | Potency: Item Level ÷ 5, +1 at grade 9, +2 at grade 10 |
| What does it cost? | Realm base × grade (Human 5 gp, Mysterious 50, Hell/Heaven 500...) |
| Can I survive in that realm? | If your Attunement is at least its Pressure |

# Profession Progression

How characters gain levels in a crafting profession (see [[FAND/Atrious/Master Professions|Master Professions]]). Profession level is separate from character level. It runs from 1 to 20, and each profession's own page lists its crafting bonus at each level.

## Learning a profession
- **Starting:** a character begins at level 1 in a new profession by spending a week with a teacher (someone at level 5 or higher in it) or by studying one of its Blueprints for a month alone.
- **How many:** any number, but only the **two highest** professions earn full Profession XP. Every other profession earns half.

## Specialties
Each of the 10 professions has **specialties**, the narrower crafts it absorbed (see [[FAND/Atrious/Master Professions|Master Professions]]). Every Blueprint has a `specialty` field.
- You start a profession with one specialty of your choice.
- Crafting outside your specialties is at disadvantage, unless the Blueprint's level is no more than half your profession level.
- You gain a specialty by finishing one item of it under a teacher who has it, or free at profession levels 5, 10, 15, and 20.
- Some specialties have extra requirements (Blood Alchemy needs fresh blood, Void Smithing needs a Void forge, and so on); each profession's page lists them.

## Profession XP
Profession XP comes from doing the work:

| Activity | XP |
|---|---|
| Craft an item (success) | 10 × the item's level |
| Craft an item (natural 20) | Double |
| Craft an item 5 or more levels below your profession level | Half |
| Failed craft | 2 × the item's level |
| Design a [[FAND/Atrious/Custom Blueprints\|Custom Blueprint]] (success) | 20 × the item's level |
| Reverse-engineer a Blueprint (success) | 15 × the item's level |
| [[FAND/Atrious/Material Refining\|Refine]] a material | 5 × the result's grade × realm tier |
| Gather a material (with the listed profession) | The material's grade × realm tier |
| Work with a material from a higher realm than you've worked before | +100, once per realm |

## Levels
To reach the next level, you need **100 × the next level** in Profession XP, counted since your last level-up.

| Level | XP to reach it | Running total |
|---|---|---|
| 2 | 200 | 200 |
| 5 | 500 | 1,400 |
| 10 | 1,000 | 5,400 |
| 15 | 1,500 | 11,900 |
| 20 | 2,000 | 20,900 |

Worked example: a level 4 Blacksmith needs 500 XP for level 5. Forging five level-10 swords (100 XP each) gets them there.

## Teachers
- A teacher at least 5 levels above you halves the XP needed for your next level. It takes a week together and costs the teacher's day rate (see [[FAND/Atrious/Economy|Economy]]: 10 gp × the teacher's level per day).
- A **Finger** or **Apostle** of a god whose Runes match the profession (for example, a Hephaestus contractor for Blacksmithing) can teach past level 15, where ordinary teachers become rare.

## Milestones
| Level | Milestone |
|---|---|
| 5 | Journeyman: may take apprentices and teach levels 1–4 |
| 10 | Can design Custom Blueprints for Rare items without disadvantage |
| 15 | Master: recognized by guilds; temples of matching gods may offer a contract |
| 20 | Grandmaster: can work Abyss-grade materials and above at a Realm Forge (see [[FAND/Atrious/Custom Blueprints\|Custom Blueprints]]) |

# Alchemy

Potions, poisons, oils, elixirs, and the blood arts: anything brewed, distilled, or drawn from a living body.

**Works with:** Blood / Organ, plants, and supplies. See Material Types in [[FAND/Atrious/Material Grading|Material Grading]].

**Blueprints:** [[FAND/Atrious/Blueprints/Alchemy.base|Alchemy Blueprints]] (563). Each Blueprint's `specialty` field shows which branch of the craft it comes from.

## Specialties
Branches of the craft. A character with this profession can make items from any specialty; the DM may require a teacher before someone tries an unfamiliar one.

### Potionmaking (283 Blueprints)
Create potions, toxins, alchemical oils, and mutagens.

*Signature creations:*
- A Lv17 draught that lets the drinker breathe fire once before it wears off (Fire).
- A Lv12 tonic that sharpens the mind enough to resist one mental intrusion (Psychic).
- A Lv7 shimmering vial that stores a single low-level spell for later use (Arcane).

### Blood Alchemy (280 Blueprints)
Use blood rituals to empower forbidden creations.

*Signature creations:*
- A Lv16 elixir that lets the drinker read a struck target's next move (Psychic).
- A Lv11 tonic that charges the blood with a single stored jolt of lightning (Lightning).
- A Lv6 draught that thickens the blood enough to slow bleeding to a crawl (Ice).

## Specialty rules
- You start a profession with **one specialty** of your choice.
- Crafting a Blueprint from a specialty you don't have is at **disadvantage**, unless its level is no more than half your profession level.
- **Gaining a specialty:** finish one item of it under a teacher who has it, or pick a new one free at profession levels 5, 10, 15, and 20.
- Each specialty also has its own requirement:

| Specialty | Needs |
|---|---|
| Potionmaking | An alchemist's kit and clean water. |
| Blood Alchemy | Fresh blood from a willing donor or a kill no more than an hour old. Most temples frown on it. |

# Blacksmithing

Working metal into weapons, armor, tools, and fittings, from village iron to the metals of Hell, Heaven, and the Void.

**Works with:** Ore / Metal. See Material Types in [[FAND/Atrious/Material Grading|Material Grading]].

**Blueprints:** [[FAND/Atrious/Blueprints/Blacksmithing.base|Blacksmithing Blueprints]] (1215). Each Blueprint's `specialty` field shows which branch of the craft it comes from.

Hell, Heaven, and Void metals need a **realm specialty**: a Blacksmith works them at disadvantage until they have finished one item of that metal under a teacher who has the specialty. The specialties are Infernal Forging (Hell), Celestial Metallurgy (Heaven), and Void Smithing (Void and Inner Void).

## Specialties
Branches of the craft. A character with this profession can make items from any specialty; the DM may require a teacher before someone tries an unfamiliar one.

### Blacksmithing (860 Blueprints)
Forge swords, heavy armor, shields, and warsteel relics.

*Signature creations:*
- A Lv16 mind-forged blade that unsettles whoever it cuts (Psychic).
- A Lv11 arcane-tempered breastplate that shrugs off a single spell each day (Arcane).
- A Lv6 venom-lined gauntlet that turns a bare-handed grapple toxic (Poison).

### Infernal Forging (111 Blueprints)
Forge with metals and materials pulled from the lower planes, at the cost of gear that always carries something of Hell in it.

*Signature creations:*
- A Lv17 Hellforged Iron Armour (Armor, Fire).
- A Lv17 Abyssal Bronze Armour (Armor, Acid).
- A Lv17 Abyssal Bronze Crossbow (Bow, Piercing).

### Celestial Metallurgy (167 Blueprints)
Work metals blessed or born beyond the Mortal Realm — starmetal, celestial gold — into gear too rare for ordinary forges.

*Signature creations:*
- A Lv20 The Unbreaking (Sword, Slashing).
- A Lv20 Celestial Gold Shortbow (Bow, Piercing).
- A Lv20 The Dawnbane Sword - Blade of Evil's Bane (Sword, Slashing).

### Void Smithing (77 Blueprints)
Forge with fragments and concepts pulled from the Void itself, producing weapons that don't behave like ordinary matter.

*Signature creations:*
- A Lv20 Ea - Sword of Rupture (Sword, Slashing).
- A Lv18 Monado - Shulk's Blade (Sword, Slashing).

## Specialty rules
- You start a profession with **one specialty** of your choice.
- Crafting a Blueprint from a specialty you don't have is at **disadvantage**, unless its level is no more than half your profession level.
- **Gaining a specialty:** finish one item of it under a teacher who has it, or pick a new one free at profession levels 5, 10, 15, and 20.
- Each specialty also has its own requirement:

| Specialty | Needs |
|---|---|
| Blacksmithing | A forge and anvil. The default specialty every Blacksmith starts with. |
| Infernal Forging | Hell metal (Brimstone Iron, Infernium, and so on) and a forge hot enough for it: a Hell vent, a Realm Forge, or a fiend-fire forge. Items carry a trace of Hell; Heaven contractors distrust them. |
| Celestial Metallurgy | Heaven metal and consecrated tools. Items can't be used to harm a celestial without the wielder taking the same damage. |
| Void Smithing | Void or Inner Void metal and a forge that burns nothing: usually a Realm Forge connected to the Void. |

# Carving

Shaping wood, stone, bone, horn, scale, crystal, and coral into bows, staffs, shields, foci, statues, and gem-set gear.

**Works with:** Wood / Plant, Stone, Bone / Fang / Horn / Scale, Crystal / Gem. See Material Types in [[FAND/Atrious/Material Grading|Material Grading]].

**Blueprints:** [[FAND/Atrious/Blueprints/Carving.base|Carving Blueprints]] (1187). Each Blueprint's `specialty` field shows which branch of the craft it comes from.

## Specialties
Branches of the craft. A character with this profession can make items from any specialty; the DM may require a teacher before someone tries an unfamiliar one.

### Woodworking (183 Blueprints)
Shape wood — ironwood, ashwood, and rarer growths — into gear that trades metal's weight for a different kind of durability.

*Signature creations:*
- A Lv13 Ironwood Hand Axe (Axe, Slashing).
- A Lv13 Ironwood Warhammer (Hammer, Bludgeoning).
- A Lv13 Ironwood Shortsword (Sword, Slashing).

### Stonecutting (76 Blueprints)
Shape raw stone into shields, tools, and fittings — the plainest and oldest of the crafting professions.

*Signature creations:*
- A Lv2 Tallow Candle Shield (Shield, Bludgeoning).

### Bone Carving (94 Blueprints)
Carve the bones of the dead and the monstrous into weapons and armor that keep a trace of what they came from.

*Signature creations:*
- A Lv17 Wraithbone Helm (Armor, Necrotic).
- A Lv17 Wraithbone Warhammer (Hammer, Bludgeoning).
- A Lv17 Wraithbone Buckler (Shield, Necrotic).

### Dragon Carving (275 Blueprints)
Use dragon parts to craft legendary artifacts.

*Signature creations:*
- A Lv19 scale-carved talisman that briefly lends the wearer a dragon's arcane resilience (Arcane).
- A Lv14 fang-carved dagger coated in a poison drawn from the scale it was cut from (Poison).
- A Lv9 carved dragon-tooth charm that keeps a small flame lit no matter the wind (Fire).

### Crystal Shaping (481 Blueprints)
Manipulate mana crystals and arcane gems.

*Signature creations:*
- A Lv16 black-crystal lens that shows a target's remaining life as a fading light (Necrotic).
- A Lv11 storm-crystal focus that stores one bolt of lightning to release later (Lightning).
- A Lv6 veined shard that weeps a slow poison when shattered (Poison).

### Tide Craft (78 Blueprints)
Work materials recovered from the sea and treated with its pressure and salt, favored for gear meant to survive the depths.

*Signature creations:*
- A Lv16 Trident of the Sea King (Staff, Bludgeoning).
- A Lv13 Deepwater Trident (Staff, Bludgeoning).
- A Lv10 Seawater-Treated Leather Armour (Armor, Piercing).

## Specialty rules
- You start a profession with **one specialty** of your choice.
- Crafting a Blueprint from a specialty you don't have is at **disadvantage**, unless its level is no more than half your profession level.
- **Gaining a specialty:** finish one item of it under a teacher who has it, or pick a new one free at profession levels 5, 10, 15, and 20.

| Specialty | Needs |

# Realm Travel

How characters get from the [[Mortal Realm]] to the other realms, what it costs, and what happens to them when they arrive. The higher a realm ranks in [[FAND/Atrious/Material Grading|Material Grading]], the harder it is to reach and the harder it is to survive in.

## Realm Pressure
Every realm pushes back on visitors who don't belong. Each realm has a **Pressure**, and each traveler has an **Attunement**.

| Realm | Pressure |
|---|---|
| Human ([[Mortal Realm]]) | 0 |
| [[Mysterious Realm\|Mysterious]] | 1 |
| [[Hell]] / [[Heaven]] | 2 |
| [[Chaos Realm\|Chaos]] | 3 |
| [[Abyss]] | 4 |
| [[Inner Realm]] | 5 |
| [[Outer Realm]] | 6 |
| [[Void]] | 7 |
| [[Inner Void]] | 8 |
| [[Primordial Realm\|Primordial]] | 9 |

**Attunement** is the highest of these:
- character level ÷ 4, rounded down;
- [[FAND/Atrious/God Contracts|contract]] rank ÷ 2, rounded down (Minor = 1 up to 1st Finger = 10);
- the Potency of a worn or carried item made with a material from that realm (see [[FAND/Atrious/Material Properties|Material Properties]]);
- the realm's own natives, and anyone invited by a god whose home realm it is, count as fully attuned.

**If Pressure is higher than Attunement**, the difference is the **strain**:

| Strain | Effect |
|---|---|
| 1 | Disadvantage on Constitution saves |
| 2 | Also gain 1 level of exhaustion at the end of each day |
| 3 | Also no benefit from long rests |
| 4+ | 1 level of exhaustion every hour. Leave quickly |

This is why gear made from a realm's own materials matters: a Hell 7 cloak (Potency 2) lets a level-4 character stand in Hell without strain.

## Ways to travel

| Method | Reaches | Requirement | Risk |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Thin places** (fog, fey rings, old mirrors) | Mysterious | Find one; Survival or Arcana DC 12 | Arrive somewhere random; time may pass differently |
| **Astral crossing** | Mysterious, Hell, Heaven, Outer | An [[FAND/Atrious/Professions/Navigation\|Navigation]] check (DC 10 + 3 × Pressure) each day | Failure: lost a day, or arrive at the wrong realm on a natural 1 |
| **A god's invitation** | That god's home realm (see [[FAND/Atrious/God Roster\|God Roster]]) | A contract of Major rank or higher, or a direct summons | None on the way; the god expects something in return |
| **Death** | Hell or Heaven | Dying; returning needs resurrection or a god's favor | Your body stays behind |
| **Gates** | Hell, Heaven | A guarded gate on the realm's border (for Hell, the [[Fiend Realm]]); a pass, a bribe, or a fight | Guards of the realm's grade |
| **Rifts** | Chaos, Abyss | A rift left by a god's death or a failed summoning; it closes in 1d6 days | No control over where you land |
| **The Fall** | Abyss | Travel down through Hell to the Rim | Falling; climbing back out is a quest |
| **Law-veins** | Inner Realm | A place where one Law is unusually strong, and a guide who knows the way (usually a contractor) | Anchor-wardens attack anyone who touches a vein |
| **Beyond the Astral** | Outer Realm | An Astral crossing that keeps going, at least a week | Pressure 6 with no rest stops |
| **Void ritual** | Void, Inner Void | A ritual using a Void-tier material as the key, consumed on use | Returning needs a second key |
| **God-falls** | Primordial | Stand where an original god died, or descend through the deepest [[Spirit Realm]] | A campaign goal, not a trip |

## Getting home
Leaving a realm uses the same methods in reverse. Carrying an **anchor**, something from the realm you want to return to, grants advantage on any check to get back there. Anyone who arrived by rift, the Fall, or death has no easy way back; getting home is its own adventure.

## Travel and crafting
- A **Realm Forge** (see [[FAND/Atrious/Custom Blueprints|Custom Blueprints]]) is always inside or connected to its realm, so Abyss-grade crafting and above means travel.
- Gathering is done in the realm itself; see each realm's Gathering page from the [[FAND/Atrious/Material Index|Material Index]].
- Contractors of Apostle rank and above can use their god's home realm as a Realm Forge.

A storm cloud forms overhead; on each of your turns you can call down a bolt of lightning to strike a point you choose within range, dealing lightning damage on a failed Dexterity save, half on a success.

**Save:** Dexterity

**At Higher Levels:** +1d10 per slot level above 3rd

*Official D&D 5e spell — SRD 5.1, © Wizards of the Coast LLC, used under CC-BY-4.0.*

# Call of the Wild

[[Nature]] — Ranger, Beast Master

Calls 1d4 friendly beasts of the caster's choosing (CR 1/4 or lower) to the caster's location, willing to fight alongside them.

Wizard, School of Conjuration

# Called Wrench

*Tertiary-tier Conjuration*

An ordinary conjuration technique, unremarkable but dependable. A single target within range must succeed on a Strength saving throw or be pushed 10ft in a direction of the caster's choice. If the movement forces it into a wall or other solid obstacle, it takes 2d6 Force damage instead of stopping short. Common enough to be found in nearly every caster's repertoire.


[[FAND/Atrious/Spells/Conjuration (School)|Conjuration]]

# Calm Blessing

*Tertiary-tier Healing*

A plain healing spell, favored for being easy to learn rather than being strong. The caster touches a willing creature (which may be themselves), granting a +2 bonus to AC until the start of the caster's next turn. Common enough to be found in nearly every caster's repertoire.


[[FAND/Atrious/Spells/Healing (School)|Healing]]

*SRD — Enchantment (official) — filed under [[FAND/Atrious/Spells/Psionics (School)|Psionics]] in this vault*

**Save:** Charisma

*Official D&D 5e spell — SRD 5.1, © Wizards of the Coast LLC, used under CC-BY-4.0.*

# Carved Sigil

*Tertiary-tier Runic Magic*

A runic magic working most journeymen pick up early and never stop using. Requires 1 minute to inscribe a seal onto a weapon, shield, or other handheld object. The next time that item is used to make an attack, it deals an extra 1d6 damage of the caster's choice, then the seal burns away. Only one seal can be active on a given item at a time. Taught early enough that almost every caster of this school knows it.

One of the more forgettable entries in psionics, but a reliable one. A single target within range must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or suffer a -2 penalty to AC until the end of its next turn. Unremarkable in every way except how often it actually gets used.


[[FAND/Atrious/Spells/Psionics (School)|Psionics]]

# Fractured Echo

*Secondary-tier Chronomancy*

A chronomancy spell reserved for casters past their earliest training. No damage, no save required — the working creates a private pocket of silence in a 15ft radius for 1 minute. Not every caster keeps this one ready — it costs more attention than most basics do.


[[FAND/Atrious/Spells/Chronomancy (School)|Chronomancy]]

# Fractured Snare

*Secondary-tier Psionics*

One of the more demanding entries in psionics's middle tier. The caster fixes on a single target within range. Unless it succeeds on a Constitution saving throw, it becomes Incapacitated until the end of its next turn. Costs real concentration, which is exactly why fewer casters bother mastering it.


[[FAND/Atrious/Spells/Psionics (School)|Psionics]]
