# 🎶 School of Resonance
*The Bard's Exclusive School of Magic*

> *"Not all spells are cast with words of power. Some are sung into being — quietly, carefully, in the spaces between heartbeats."*
> — Mistress Vael, College of the Singing Wound

[[FAND/Atrious/Spells/Spell Index|Spell Index]] · [[FAND/Atrious/Classes/Bard|Bard]]

---

## Overview

The School of Resonance is a unique form of magic accessible **only to Bards**. Unlike conventional spellcasting, Resonance magic requires the caster to perform a specific **Verbal Chant** (their *Resonance Phrase*) before or during casting. In exchange for this limitation, Resonance spells are:

- **Subtle** — they register as no school to Detect Magic
- **Stacking** — effects can linger and compound with other Bard abilities
- **Non-expending** — some Resonance cantrips do not consume Bardic Inspiration dice

However, Resonance spells have **reduced potency** compared to equivalent spells from other schools. They trade raw power for flexibility and stealth.

---

## How Resonance Works

### The Chant Requirement

Every Resonance spell requires the caster to speak, hum, or sing their **Resonance Phrase** — a personal verbal sequence that varies by bard. This phrase:
- Must be audible to the caster (does not need to be heard by others at low volume)
- Takes the form of **V (Verbal)** component but is *always required*, even for spells that would normally allow S-only casting
- Can be incorporated into performance, speech, or background music without drawing attention — DC 12 Deception or Performance check

> **If Silenced:** A Bard under the Silence spell or equivalent cannot cast any Resonance magic. This is Resonance's primary weakness.

### Resonance Phrases

Each Bard develops their own unique phrase. Work with your DM to establish yours. Examples:

| Style | Example Phrase |
|-------|----------------|
| Ancient Tongue | *"Vas en kural, mii sorath"* |
| Melodic | Three descending notes, hummed softly |
| Rhythmic | A specific drum pattern tapped on the chest |
| Spoken | *"Still the world, bend the veil"* |
| Breath-pattern | An inhale-hold-exhale rhythm |

---

## Resonance Spells by Level

### Cantrips

#### Lingering Note
- **Casting Time:** 1 Action (Chant required)
- **Range:** 60ft
- **Duration:** Concentration, up to 1 minute
- **Components:** V, S
- **Effect:** You weave a barely audible tone into the air. One creature of your choice within range must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or suffer **disadvantage on Concentration checks** for the duration. Creatures that cannot hear are immune. This registers as no school of magic.
- *Lower potency than Hold Person but costs no spell slot at Cantrip rank.*

#### Echoing Whisper
- **Casting Time:** 1 Action (Chant required)
- **Range:** 30ft
- **Duration:** Until dispelled or triggered
- **Components:** V
- **Effect:** You implant a short phrase (up to 10 words) into a surface, object, or doorway. The phrase plays back aloud — in your voice — when a creature you specify passes within 5ft. Only you can perceive the implanted phrase before it triggers; it is otherwise invisible to Detect Magic.
- *Useful for messaging, alarms, or ambushes.*

#### Fading Chord
- **Casting Time:** 1 Bonus Action (Chant required)
- **Range:** Self
- **Duration:** 1 round
- **Components:** V
- **Effect:** Until the start of your next turn, your voice and any music you produce cannot be traced to a source — listeners cannot determine where the sound originates. You gain advantage on Performance and Deception checks that involve misdirection through sound.

---

### Level 1

#### Sympathetic Resonance
- **Casting Time:** 1 Action (Chant required)
- **Range:** Touch
- **Duration:** Concentration, up to 10 minutes
- **Components:** V, S
- **Damage:** None
- **Effect:** You establish a resonant link between two willing creatures (one of which may be yourself). For the duration, each creature is aware of the emotional state of the other — not thoughts, only feelings. Additionally, once per round as a free action, you may spend 1 Bardic Inspiration die to transfer up to 5 hit points from one linked creature to the other (no action required from the recipient).
- *A subtle support tool. The healing is minor but costs no action.*

#### Dissonant Hum
- **Casting Time:** 1 Action (Chant required)
- **Range:** 30ft cone
- **Duration:** Instantaneous
- **Components:** V
- **Damage:** 1d6 Psychic
- **Save:** Constitution, half damage
- **Effect:** You emit a short dissonant burst. Creatures in the cone take **1d6 Psychic damage** and must succeed on a CON save or be **Distracted** until the end of their next turn (disadvantage on the next attack roll or ability check they make).
- *Scales: +1d6 per spell slot above 1st. Max 5d6 at 5th slot.*
- *Weaker than Vicious Mockery but affects all creatures in cone.*

#### Borrowed Tempo
- **Casting Time:** 1 Reaction (Chant required; triggered when an ally rolls Initiative)
- **Range:** 60ft
- **Duration:** 1 minute
- **Components:** V
- **Effect:** When a creature within range rolls Initiative, you may use your Reaction to sing a fragment of tempo into them. They gain a +2 bonus to their Initiative roll. Additionally, on their first turn in combat, they may take one additional 5ft movement without triggering opportunity attacks.
- *A subtle combat opener — gives allies a slight positional and Initiative edge.*

---

### Level 2

#### Harmonic Anchor
- **Casting Time:** 1 Action (Chant required)
- **Range:** 60ft
- **Duration:** Concentration, up to 1 minute
- **Components:** V, S
- **Effect:** You fix a creature's position in harmonic space. The target must succeed on a Strength saving throw or be **Resonance Locked** — it cannot be forcibly moved (pushed, pulled, teleported) for the duration, though it can still move willingly. While locked, it also has resistance to Thunder damage.
- *Lower potency than Hold Person — the creature can still act freely. But the lock is hard to break externally.*

#### Woven Lullaby
- **Casting Time:** 1 Action (Chant required)
- **Range:** 30ft
- **Duration:** Concentration, up to 1 minute
- **Components:** V
- **Save:** Wisdom
- **Effect:** You weave a thread of drowsiness into the ambient sound around one creature. The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or have its speed reduced by 10ft and suffer a **-2 penalty to Perception checks** for the duration. On a failed save by 5 or more, the creature is also **Incapacitated** for 1 round before recovering.
- *Compared to Sleep — this affects one creature of any HP, but the effect is softer.*

#### Sound Mirror
- **Casting Time:** 1 Action (Chant required)
- **Range:** Self
- **Duration:** Concentration, up to 10 minutes
- **Components:** V, S
- **Effect:** You create a magical duplicate of your own voice that sounds from a location you can see within 60ft. You can use a Bonus Action on subsequent turns to move the duplicate up to 30ft. The duplicate can speak, whisper, or sing at any volume you choose. Detect Magic reveals nothing unusual — this spell produces no magical signature.
- *Useful for misdirection, communication, and performance.*

---

### Level 3

#### Resonant Fracture
- **Casting Time:** 1 Action (Chant required)
- **Range:** 60ft
- **Duration:** Instantaneous
- **Components:** V, S
- **Damage:** 3d8 Thunder
- **Save:** Constitution, half damage
- **Effect:** You strike a single creature with a focused resonant pulse. On a hit, the target takes **3d8 Thunder damage** and must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failure, any Concentration spell they are maintaining immediately ends.
- *Scales: +2d8 per slot level above 3rd.*
- *The Concentration-break is the real weapon here. Weaker raw damage than Thunderwave, but targeted and devastating against casters.*

#### Layered Cadence
- **Casting Time:** 1 Minute (Chant required; this is a ritual)
- **Range:** 30ft radius
- **Duration:** 8 hours
- **Components:** V, S, M *(a tuning fork or instrument string worth at least 5gp)*
- **Effect:** You spend one minute establishing a resonant frequency in a location. For the duration, all creatures you designate within the area gain a +1 bonus to saving throws and cannot be surprised. You are aware (as a vague sense) whenever a new creature enters the area, even while asleep.
- *A camp-protection ritual. Weak bonus, but no action cost after setup.*

#### Countermelody
- **Casting Time:** 1 Reaction (Chant required; triggered when you see a spell being cast within 60ft)
- **Range:** 60ft
- **Duration:** Instantaneous
- **Components:** V
- **Effect:** When a creature within range casts a spell, you may use your Reaction to weave a countermelody. The caster must succeed on a **Charisma saving throw** (DC = your spell save DC) or their spell is cast at **disadvantage** — if the spell requires an attack roll, the roll is made with disadvantage; if it requires targets to save, they save with advantage this turn.
- *Compared to Counterspell — this doesn't cancel the spell, but it significantly weakens it. No spell slot required.*

---

### Level 4

#### Dissonant Veil
- **Casting Time:** 1 Action (Chant required)
- **Range:** Self (20ft radius)
- **Duration:** Concentration, up to 10 minutes
- **Components:** V
- **Effect:** You fill the area around you with subtle dissonant harmonics. Hostile creatures within the area have disadvantage on Perception checks that rely on hearing. Additionally, spells cast within the area that have a verbal component must succeed on a DC 13 Concentration check or fail, as the dissonance interrupts spellcasting.
- *An area denial tool — particularly brutal in enclosed spaces. Weaker than Silence because it doesn't fully prevent casting.*

#### Resonance Echo
- **Casting Time:** 1 Action (Chant required)
- **Range:** Touch
- **Duration:** 24 hours
- **Components:** V, S
- **Effect:** You touch a willing creature and bind a faint echo of a spell to their aura. Choose one Bard Resonance cantrip you know. For the duration, the target creature can cast that cantrip once — as if they were a Bard — without needing to know the Resonance Phrase. They use your spell save DC. After casting it, the echo fades.
- *A gift spell. Lets you lend a cantrip to an ally for a day.*

---

### Level 5

#### The Grand Chord
- **Casting Time:** 1 Action (Chant required; this is your Resonance Phrase spoken in full at maximum volume)
- **Range:** 90ft
- **Duration:** Concentration, up to 1 minute
- **Components:** V, S
- **Effect:** You strike a resonant chord that shakes reality. All creatures of your choice within 90ft must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failure, they are **Resonance Bound** for the duration — their emotions are flattened, their will suppressed. A Resonance Bound creature:
  - Cannot cast spells that require Verbal components
  - Has disadvantage on Charisma checks and saving throws
  - Takes **2d6 Psychic damage** at the start of each of their turns
  - May repeat the saving throw at the end of each of their turns

  On a success, the creature takes **2d6 Psychic damage** only.
- *This is Resonance's "big spell" — broadly effective but requires concentration and the open chant gives it away completely.*

---

## Design Philosophy

Resonance magic is intentionally **subtle and support-oriented**. It punishes silence and rewards positioning and preparation. A Bard specialising in Resonance is:

- A **battlefield manipulator** who weakens enemies rather than destroying them
- A **camp utility specialist** — setup rituals, communication tools, protective harmonics
- **Dependent on their voice** — their greatest vulnerability

When Silenced, a Resonance Bard loses *all* of this school. Plan accordingly.

---

## College Synergies

Resonance spells synergise with:
- **College of the Iron Drum** — Resonance damage spells gain a Thunder rider
- **College of the Silent Bell** — Resonance spells can be cast silently, breaking the Silence limitation once per long rest
- **College of the Broken Lute** — Resonance cantrips cost no Bardic Inspiration when cast at emotional peak

*(These three Colleges are not yet written up as full subclasses in this vault — noted here as hooks for a future subclass pass.)*

# Spell Index

Three layers live side by side in each school below (each is one Obsidian Base / database view, filterable by everything including the `tags:` tier marker):

1. **Original content** — hand-written or generated from my own word banks and templates, not sourced from the Atrious archive's generated volumes. Tagged `cantrip`/`tertiary`/`secondary`/`primary` by tier.
2. **Real D&D 5e spells (SRD)** — the official open-licensed spell list, remapped from D&D's 8 official schools into whichever of this vault's 20 schools actually fits the spell's theme. Marked `tier: "SRD"` and tagged `srd`. Two sub-batches:
   - **SRD 5.1 core** (350 spells) — the 2014-era open list: Fireball, Magic Missile, Cure Wounds, and the rest.
   - **SRD 5.2 additions** (35 spells) — the batch WotC folded into the open license in 2024, including former Xanathar's/Tasha's-exclusive favorites (Booming Blade, Absorb Elements, the Summon X spells, etc.).
3. **DLC-inspired originals** (25 spells) — mechanical concepts drawn from well-known non-SRD supplement spells (Xanathar's, Tasha's, Fizban's), but with original names, flavor, and reworded effects rather than WotC's actual text — the same treatment used for the vault-wide named-spell cleanup. Marked `tier: "Original"`, tagged by tier like the rest of the original content. These are *not* SRD-licensed content since nothing verbatim was copied; they're original spells that happen to share a mechanical idea with a real one.

> **Attribution:** This work includes material from the System Reference Document 5.1 and 5.2 ("SRD") by Wizards of the Coast LLC, available at https://dnd.wizards.com/resources/systems-reference-document, licensed under CC-BY-4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/legalcode). Descriptions are paraphrased, not verbatim, and spells are reclassified into this vault's own school system. The DLC-inspired originals (category 3 above) are separate, original works — no WotC text or names were copied for those.

**Pyramid structure per school (original content only):** Cantrip (unlimited-use, no slot, ~15 per school) → Tertiary (common, levels 1-3, ~40-60 per school) → Secondary (levels 4-6, ~25 per school) → Primary (rare, levels 7-9, ~10 per school, each tied to one specific named Rune and requiring a genuine Primary-tier acquisition per [[Class]]).

# Spell Slots

How many spell slots a character has at each level, split by caster type. Follows the standard 5e chassis, same as every class in this vault (see each [[FAND/Atrious/Classes/Sorcerer|Class]] page).

The key thing to note: **pure magic classes get noticeably more at level 1 than everyone else** — a Full Caster starts with 3 first-level slots at character level 1 (bumped up from the standard 5e value of 2, a deliberate house rule for this vault), while a Half Caster gets *zero* spell slots until level 2. That gap is intentional and carries through this vault — being *only* a magic class is the tradeoff that earns the faster progression.

### Exception: Artificer
[[FAND/Atrious/Classes/Artificer|Artificer]] is technically a Half Caster but rounds its caster level *up* instead of down, so unlike Paladin/Ranger it gets 2 first-level slots starting at character level 1 — the only Half Caster that keeps pace with Full Casters at the very start.

## Pact Magic (unique)
[[FAND/Atrious/Classes/Warlock|Warlock]]

Not on the same track as the tables above. Warlock slots are always cast at the Warlock's highest available slot level, there are far fewer of them, and — unlike every other caster — they recover on a **short rest**, not a long rest.

## Non-Casters
[[FAND/Atrious/Classes/Barbarian|Barbarian]], [[FAND/Atrious/Classes/Fighter|Fighter]], [[FAND/Atrious/Classes/Monk|Monk]], [[FAND/Atrious/Classes/Rogue|Rogue]]

No spell slots from the base class. Two subclasses graft a Third Caster progression on top of these (Eldritch Knight for Fighter, Arcane Trickster for Rogue) — those follow yet another table, sitting between Half Caster and no casting at all, and only reach 4th-level slots by character level 20.

## Overview

## Theme
Unlocked by acquisition rather than level, following the [[Class]] system's Primary/Secondary/Tertiary tiers. A Diamond Patron warlock treats Diamond himself, not [[Gnome]], as the progenitor.

## Acquisition Tiers
- **Primary** — an actual shard of [[Diamond]]'s shattered body. Lets the warlock harden any part of themselves to true diamond hardness for a moment, enough to no-sell a single hit rather than just blunt it.
- **Secondary** — something Diamond wore or shaped before he was broken, rather than a piece of him directly. Lets the warlock refract light off their own skin, hard enough to blind at close range.
- **Tertiary** — anything else cut from or shaped like diamond, real or cheap imitation. Raises power only, no unique ability.

# Sylph Bloodline

## Overview
Sylph Bloodline is a Sorcerous Origin for the [[FAND/Atrious/Classes/Sorcerer|Sorcerer]] class, tracing its power to [[Air]] and the dead air spirit [[Sylph]].

## Theme
Unlocked by acquisition rather than level, following the [[Class]] system's Primary/Secondary/Tertiary tiers.

## Acquisition Tiers
- **Primary** — a piece of [[Sylph]]'s own remains. Lets the sorcerer fall as slowly as they like, landing from any height without being hurt by it.
- **Secondary** — a relic tied to one of Sylph's children — [[Boreas]], [[Zephyrus]], [[Notus]], [[Eurus]], or [[Vortex]] itself — rather than Sylph directly. Grants a small taste of that specific child's own power rather than plain wind.
- **Tertiary** — anything else touched by [[Air]]: ordinary wind, a feather, open sky. Raises power only, no unique ability.

Unlocked by acquisition rather than level, following the [[Class]] system's Primary/Secondary/Tertiary tiers.

## Acquisition Tiers
- **Primary** — a piece of [[Undine]]'s own remains. Lets the sorcerer breathe and see clearly underwater without needing to cast anything for it.
- **Secondary** — a relic tied to [[Ice]] or [[Frost]] rather than Undine directly. Keeps a thin permanent layer of ice across the sorcerer's skin, blunting blows before any Water is even cast.
- **Tertiary** — anything else touched by [[Water]]: ordinary rain, a filled waterskin, damp cloth. Raises power only, no unique ability.

# FAND Development Summary

Everything built in the FAND vault since the Patch Notes began, organized by system. Version-by-version detail is in the [[FAND/Patch Notes|Patch Notes]] database. Current version: **1.24** (2026-10-04).

## At a glance

| Area | Now |
|---|---|
| Subclasses | 163, all official PHB, Xanathar's, Tasha's, and SCAG ones plus three from the 2024 PHB, alongside the homebrew Rune subclasses |
| Professions | 10 broad professions, absorbing the 31 old crafts as specialties |
| Blueprints | 6,503 in the vault and 6,550 in FAND.html |
| Spells | About 2,330, all with classes filled in; 73 converted to healing and support |
| Materials | 1,597 graded materials, each with a property, price, and its own note |
| Monsters | 103 homebrew with full stats, plus 643 official D&D monsters |
| Realms | 11 realm tiers, each with lore, a Bestiary, and a Gathering page |
| Gods | 70 gods with Runes, realms, signature materials, and 201 named Fingers |
| Rules pages | Armor Class, Material Grading, Material Properties, Material Refining, Custom Blueprints, Crafting, Economy, Profession Progression, God Contracts, Realm Travel, Monster Stats |
| Player-facing | Player's Guide, Profession Quick Reference, Realm Map |
| Tools | FAND.html app; GitHub repo with generator and check scripts |

## Classes and subclasses
- **Official subclasses:** 58 official subclasses were added as paraphrased summaries labeled with their source book (v1.03). Three new 2024 PHB subclasses followed: Path of the World Tree, College of Dance, and Circle of the Sea (v1.18).
- **2024 revisions:** each class page notes which of its subclasses the 2024 Player's Handbook revised, and that every class picks its subclass at level 3.
- **Spell classes:** every spell now lists classes. Pyramid spells get them from their school, plus the class tied to their Rune where one applies (v1.17).

## Armor Class (v1.04–v1.06)
- **How AC works:** [[FAND/Atrious/Armor Class|Armor Class]] starts at 0 and is built from Constitution, natural traits, armor, shields, and magic.
- **Damage reduction:** AC reduces damage in reverse tax brackets on a 1/x curve, AC ÷ (AC + 30). It never reaches 100%, and every hit deals at least 1 damage.
- **Crits:** headshots are critical hits, ×1.5 damage before AC.
- **Natural vs. Gear AC:** Natural AC can't be looted. Gear AC can, but looted armor is Damaged until it's repaired.
- **AC on Blueprints:** all 837 armor and shield Blueprints have an AC value, armor type, and slot. Slots are Body, Head, Hands, Feet, Shoulders, and Back; shields come in Buckler, Shield, and Tower.

## Materials and crafting
- **[[FAND/Atrious/Material Grading|Material Grading]] (v1.07):** every material has a realm and a grade from 1 to 10. That gives a Material Rank (1–100), which sets an Item Level (1–50).

  | Tier | Realm |
  |---|---|
  | 1 | Human |
  | 2 | Mysterious |
  | 3 | Hell / Heaven |
  | 4 | Chaos |
  | 5 | Abyss |
  | 6 | Inner Realm |
  | 7 | Outer Realm |
  | 8 | Void |
  | 9 | Inner Void |
  | 10 | Primordial |

- **Grading (v1.10):** all existing Blueprint materials are graded, and Blueprints record their strongest material.
- **[[FAND/Atrious/Material Properties|Material Properties]] (v1.13, v1.18):** every material gives a property, 48 in all, such as Shapeshifting, Sovereign of the Dead, Eye Ray, Burning, and Piercing Edge. Strength scales with Potency (1–10), and grade 9–10 materials get a boost.
- **Materials database (v1.14):** one note per material in an Obsidian Base. Each note has its realm, grade, rank, Item Level, rarity, type, property, Potency, source, and price.
- **[[FAND/Atrious/Material Index|Material Index]]:** all materials listed by realm.
- **[[FAND/Atrious/Material Refining|Material Refining]] (v1.17):** three materials of one grade make one of the next grade. Moving up to the next realm takes five, a binding agent, and a Realm Forge.
- **[[FAND/Atrious/Custom Blueprints|Custom Blueprints]] (v1.07):** players design their own items from a primary material and up to two secondaries, then pass a design check. Traits come from the materials' properties. There's a template and a `Blueprints/Custom/` folder for player-made items.
- **Blueprint properties (v1.18):** 1,925 weapons, armor pieces, and shields carry the property of their strongest material.
- **[[FAND/Atrious/Economy|Economy]] (v1.20):** a material's price is its realm base × grade, and Void-grade materials and above aren't sold. The page also covers where to buy and sell, Blueprint prices, crafting labor, services, and contract tithes.

## Professions
- **Ten professions (v1.21):** the 31 old crafts became 10. Each old craft is now a specialty kept on its profession's page.

  | Profession | Absorbed |
  |---|---|
  | Blacksmithing | Infernal Forging, Celestial Metallurgy, Void Smithing |
  | Carving | Woodworking, Stonecutting, Bone Carving, Dragon Carving, Crystal Shaping, Tide Craft |
  | Tailoring | Arcane Tailoring, Shadow Weaving |
  | Alchemy | Potionmaking, Blood Alchemy |
  | Cooking | Spirit Cooking |
  | Enchanting | Sigilcraft, Glyph Inscription, Soul Binding, Elemental Binding, Relic Restoration |
  | Engineering | Clockwork Engineering, Golemancy, Siege Engineering, Building, Masonry |
  | Harvesting | Farming, Beast Taming, plus the new Mining and Foraging |
  | Scavenging | Scavenger |
  | Navigation | Astral Navigation |

- **Blueprint fields:** every Blueprint has a `profession` and a `specialty` field.
- **Harvesting and Scavenging (v1.23):** Harvesting gathers ore, stone, crystal, and plants. Scavenging strips hide, bone, blood, organs, and essences from corpses.
- **[[FAND/Atrious/Profession Progression|Profession Progression]] (v1.20):** Profession XP from crafting, designing, refining, and gathering, with teachers and milestones.
- **Specialty rules (v1.23):** you start with one specialty and gain more over time. Crafting outside your specialties is at disadvantage, and each specialty has its own requirement.
- **Realm specialties:** Hell, Heaven, and Void metals need a Blacksmith with the matching realm specialty.
- **[[FAND/Atrious/Profession Quick Reference|Profession Quick Reference]] (v1.23):** example Blueprints for each profession at levels 1, 5, 10, 15, and 20.
- **More Blueprints for the newer professions:** 177 across v1.17 and v1.20, and 59 Scavenging tools in v1.23.
- **Cleanup (v1.23):** 26 duplicates merged and names tidied. Same-stat variants (1,632 Blueprints) link each other in their descriptions.

## Monsters and realms
- **Realm lore (v1.09):** pages for the Mortal, Mysterious, Chaos, Abyss, Inner, and Primordial Realms. The pages for Hell, Heaven, the Outer Realm, the Void, and the Inner Void already existed.
- **Bestiaries (v1.10–v1.12):** one per realm.
  - **Homebrew:** 103 monsters with drops.
  - **Official:** 643 D&D monsters from the Monster Manual, Volo's, Mordenkainen's, Fizban's, and Glory of the Giants. Each has its CR, a grade from that CR, a description in my own words, and graded drops. There are no stat blocks.
- **Gathering pages (v1.10):** ores, plants, and crystals for each realm.
- **[[FAND/Atrious/Monster Stats|Monster Stats]] (v1.20):**
  - **Homebrew:** each monster has a level, HP, Natural AC, attacks, a save DC, and a signature trait from its best drop. Grade 10 monsters have boss rules.
  - **Official:** monsters convert to this AC system with Natural AC = 2 × (book AC − 10) + CR.
- **[[FAND/Atrious/Realm Travel|Realm Travel]] (v1.17):**
  - **Pressure vs. Attunement:** each realm has a Pressure from 0 to 9. A traveler's Attunement comes from their level, contract rank, or realm-material gear. If Pressure is higher, the traveler suffers strain.
  - **Getting there:** 11 travel methods, and an anchor from home makes the return trip easier.
- **[[FAND/Atrious/Realm Map|Realm Map]] (v1.20):** a diagram of every route between realms.

## Gods
- **[[FAND/Atrious/God Contracts|God Contracts]] (v1.08, v1.15):** ten ranks, from Minor up to 1st Finger, and the five Fingers form the god's Hand. Each rank has spells, Natural AC, duties, and a reward ladder. There are rules for rising in rank, staying loyal to one god, breaking a contract, and what happens when a god dies.

# v1.04 — Armor Class rework

*2026-09-26 · Armor Class*

**Added**
- [[FAND/Atrious/Armor Class|Armor Class]] rules page, linked from [[FAND]].

**Changed**
- AC now starts at 0 and is built from Constitution, natural traits, armor, shields, and magic. Armor and shields give AC based on their Blueprint level.
- AC is damage reduction as a percentage: damage × 30 / (30 + AC). Before, AC was subtracted from damage, so hits had to scale exponentially to get through high AC.
- Headshots (crits) stay ×1.5, applied before AC.
- AC is split into Natural AC (can't be looted) and Gear AC (can be looted). Looted armor starts Damaged at half AC until repaired through a profession, and gives half AC to a wearer below its level.

---

# v1.05 — Reverse-tax-bracket damage reduction

*2026-09-26 · Armor Class*

**Changed**
- [[FAND/Atrious/Armor Class|Armor Class]]: damage reduction now works as reverse tax brackets. Each higher bracket of AC blocks less per point (2.5% per point for the first 10 AC, 1.5% for the next 10, and so on), following the 1/x curve AC / (AC + 30).
- Reduction approaches 100% but never reaches it, and every hit deals at least 1 damage. Added a bracket table with a worked example.

The bottomless dark below [[Hell]], where anything that falls keeps falling. It's tier 5 (**Abyss**) in [[FAND/Atrious/Material Grading|Material Grading]]. It's the first realm above the power range of the ordinary Blueprints, and the realm of the [[FAND/Atrious/Demons/Demon Princes — The Abyss|Demon Princes]].

**D&D class:** — a realm, not a class.

## Overview
Hell is built on rules, contracts, and ranks. The Abyss is what's underneath those rules: a vertical realm with no floor, made of endless layers. Each layer is a realm of its own shaped by whoever rules it. The Demon Princes hold the largest layers and war with each other without end. Their wars are one of the few things Hell's devils and Heaven's gods agree on: better down there than up here.

## Regions
- **The Rim:** where the Abyss meets the bottom of Hell. Devils guard it to keep demons from climbing up.
- **The Layers:** hundreds of stacked realms, one per ruler. Examples include the Shattered Realm (triple-layered, ruled by Xazareth), the Drowned Deep (Bathyrax), and the Silken Court (Velsara).
- **The Fall:** the open dark between layers. You can fall through it for days.

## Inhabitants
Demons of every kind, the [[FAND/Atrious/Demons/Demon Princes — The Abyss|Demon Princes]] and their courts, and the lightless leviathans that swim the Fall.

## Getting there
Down through Hell, or through a rift opened by a demon summoning gone wrong. There's no easy way back up. Climbing is the main danger.

## Materials (Abyss 1–10)
Drowned iron, Abyss pearl, deepmaw tooth, lightless-leviathan scale. From here upward, crafting needs a **Realm Forge** (see [[FAND/Atrious/Custom Blueprints|Custom Blueprints]]). The most famous one is a forge on the Rim that devils and demons both claim.

## Dangers
Falling forever. Demon lords who collect mortals the way gods collect contractors. Darkness that drains light sources.

## Adventure hooks
- A Demon Prince is offering a contract to anyone who can bring back a rival's heart (Abyss 10).
- The Rim forge has changed hands again, and whoever holds it now is taking commissions.

## Related
- [[Hell]] · [[Chaos Realm]] · [[Inner Realm]]
- [[FAND/Atrious/Demons/Demon Princes — The Abyss|Demon Princes — The Abyss]]
- [[FAND/Atrious/Material Grading|Material Grading]]

## Overview
Chaos is [[Dark]]'s answer to [[Serenity]]. It's a Law that resists stillness. Where its Rune power pooled after a god's death, it turned a whole region into a place that can't hold its shape. Mountains turn liquid, rivers run upward, and a road is only a road until you stop looking at it. Hell and Heaven are at least *ordered*, even if the order is cruel. The Chaos Realm has no order at all, which is why it ranks above both.

## Regions
- **The Churn:** the outer band, where change is slow enough to survive for a few days.
- **Stormglass flats:** plains of glass fused by storms that change element every hour.
- **The Unmade Core:** the center, where nothing stays the same from one breath to the next. No confirmed visitor has come back.

## Inhabitants
Warpbeasts whose bodies change as they move, chaos-spawn, and the occasional [[FAND/Atrious/Subclasses/Wild Magic (Sorcerer)|Wild Magic]] sorcerer looking for the source of their power.

## Getting there
Wild-magic surges, broken rifts left by the death of a Chaos-aligned god, or simply walking far enough into a region that has started to warp.

## Materials (Chaos 1–10)
Shifting ore, stormglass, warpbeast hide, chaos-spawn eyes. Items made from Chaos materials deal a random damage type each hit (see [[FAND/Atrious/Custom Blueprints|Custom Blueprints]]).

## Dangers
Your equipment, spells, and even your body can change without warning. The DM may roll a wild surge whenever a character rests here.

To gain a class tied to a specific Law, a mortal has to acquire something closely bound to that Law's progenitor — the god or Spirit the Law actually comes from — rather than simply learning to cast it. What's acquired falls into three tiers, and the closer the tier, the more the class's power grows:

- **Primary** — a direct piece of the progenitor itself: a body part, blood, or fragment of the entity the Law was pulled from. A shard of [[Diamond]]'s shattered body would count as Primary toward a Diamond class, the same way a piece of [[Ignis]] itself would toward Fire.
- **Secondary** — something once removed from the progenitor: an item it made, wore, or passed down to a child Law rather than the entity itself. A relic of [[Iron]], [[Gnome]]'s first child, would count as Secondary toward an Earth-lineage class rather than Primary.
- **Tertiary** — everything else with a thematic link but no real lineage to the progenitor: an object simply shaped from or touched by the Law, like an ordinary [[Blade]] forged from [[Steel]] rather than anything pulled from [[Iron]] or [[Gnome]] directly.

Primary acquisitions are rare enough that most are gone with their progenitors or locked away — [[Iron]] himself is still stuck in the spirit realm, for instance — which is why almost every class an ordinary mortal ends up with is built on nothing better than a Tertiary link.

Tertiary only raises a class's power, since there's rarely enough of the progenitor left in it to shape into anything specific. Primary and Secondary are different: the exact piece acquired unlocks an ability unique to it, so no two Primary or Secondary relics grant quite the same thing.

## Overview
When a god dies and its power breaks into Runes, those Runes still have to hold onto *something*. The Inner Realm is where they hold on. It's a vast structure of anchors, veins, and roots under every realm. The Laws run through it like ore through rock. Damage it, and a Law weakens everywhere at once. Gods know this, so the Inner Realm is heavily guarded and rarely spoken of.

## Regions
- **The Law-veins:** tunnels where raw Law runs visibly through the rock. Each vein carries a single Law.
- **The Anchor Halls:** chambers holding the anchors of the most important Laws, each guarded by an anchor-warden.
- **The Root:** the deepest point, where every vein meets. It's said to sit directly against the [[Void]].

## Inhabitants
Anchor-wardens (ancient constructs whose makers no one remembers), Law-beasts that feed on raw veins, and a few [[FAND/Atrious/God Contracts|Fingers]] sent by gods to guard, or quietly steal, what's anchored here.

## Getting there
Only through deep places where a Law is unusually strong, or with the help of a god's contractor who already knows the way.

## Materials (Inner Realm 1–10)
Law-vein ore, anchorstone, anchor-warden plate, coreheart crystal. Mining a Law-vein weakens that Law slightly, everywhere. Crafters are expected to know this and do it anyway.

## Dangers
Anchor-wardens attack anyone who touches a vein. Raw Law can overwrite the mind of whoever gets too close.

## Adventure hooks
- A Law is weakening across the Mortal Realm, and someone is mining its vein.
- A god wants a specific anchor moved closer to its own realm.

## Overview
The Mortal Realm is the middle ground that [[Heaven]] and [[Hell]] mirror each other across. It has almost no Laws of its own. Nearly all of its magic comes from Runes left by dead gods and from contracts and pacts with living ones. That makes mortals weak, but also useful: a god grows by getting others to follow its Law, and the Mortal Realm holds more potential followers than any other realm.

## Regions
- **Settled lands:** kingdoms, cities, and farmland. This is where most worship and most succession wars happen, and gods bet on both.
- **Wilds:** forests, mountains, and seas with ordinary beasts and the occasional stray from a higher realm.
- **Thin places:** spots where the [[Astral]], [[Mirror Realm]], or [[Fiend Realm]] press close. Most mortal contact with other realms starts at one.

## Inhabitants
Humans and the other mortal peoples, beasts, and monsters born here. Also [[FAND/Atrious/God Contracts|contractors]] of every god, all quietly working against each other.

## Materials (Human 1–10)
Iron, steel, silver, ordinary woods and hides at the low end. Starfall iron and wyvern scale at the top. See [[FAND/Atrious/Material Grading|Material Grading]].

## Dangers
Being mortal: other gods' contractors, devils offering [[Pacts]], and things from higher realms that slip through thin places.

## Overview
The Mysterious Realm isn't one place. It's every pocket, fold, and edge where reality goes thin without fully breaking. Scholars group them together because they share three traits:
- time and distance don't behave quite right there;
- things there are half-real;
- no god has ever managed to claim one for long.

## Regions
- **The [[Astral]]:** the thin space between realms that gods and spirits pass through.
- **The [[Mirror Realm]]:** pockets born from [[Reflection]] used too often in one place. They show a version of the Mortal Realm that answers back.
- **Fey pockets:** hidden groves and courts where seasons and moods have more weight than physics.
- **Spirit edges:** the outer rim of the [[Spirit Realm]], where lesser spirits drift. It's far from the progenitor remains in its depths.

## Inhabitants
Wisps, fey, reflections that have gained a will of their own, wandering spirits, and mortals who got lost and stayed.

## Getting there
Mostly by accident: a thin place, a mirror, a fey ring, or a wrong turn in fog. Leaving is harder than arriving.

## Materials (Mysterious 1–10)
Wisp glow-glands, moonsilver, mirror shards, fey silk, astral dust, fey stag antler.

## Dangers
Losing time: a night inside can be a year outside. Your own reflection trying to swap places with you. Fey bargains that are technically fair.

## Adventure hooks
- A village's mirrors have all started showing the same stranger.
- A fey court offers a Mysterious 9 material in exchange for a name.

Raising a corpse only needs the corpse itself — no [[Pacts]] deal — but success isn't guaranteed. The chance depends on how the corpse's level compares to the necromancer's own: a corpse at your level succeeds 2 times in 10, following (2/10)^(corpse level − your level + 1). Each level the corpse sits above you multiplies the difficulty by another 2/10, while a corpse even one level below you already clears the formula past 100%, making the attempt a guaranteed success.

Like every other [[Class]], becoming a Necromancer isn't just a matter of learning the [[Curse]] — it means acquiring something tied to the practice's progenitor, and that progenitor isn't a Spirit or a god. It's the very first mortal who ever became a [[Lich]], proving a corpse and Spirit could be bound into undeath at all rather than simply returned through [[Life]] or [[Death]] outright.
- **Primary** — an actual piece of the First Lich's remains, vanishingly rare since a Lich rarely dies cleanly enough to leave anything behind to find. Its unique ability works the same way [[Character Death]] already does for anyone — the wielder keeps playing as the same character instead of losing them, and chooses which stat takes the -1 instead of it always hitting their highest — except the loss isn't permanent: it heals back the next time they successfully raise a corpse of their own.
- **Secondary** — one of the First Lich's own creations, some ancient [[Death knight]] or [[Dullahan]] still bound to its will centuries later. Its unique ability binds that specific undead directly to the necromancer instead of raising a new one, handing over a subordinate that kept its full skill rather than the fraction any freshly-raised corpse would.
- **Tertiary** — everything else: any ordinary [[Corpse]], [[Bones]], or [[Curse]]-inscribed material, which is why nearly every necromancer alive today is building their Class on nothing better than this.

## Overview
Every god alive today is a replica built from the power of gods who came before (see [[Runes]]). The Primordial Realm holds the originals: the progenitors whose bodies became the Laws, and the first gods, of whom [[Infinatas]] is one of the last still standing. Most of it lies in the deepest parts of the [[Spirit Realm]], far below the edges that lesser spirits drift through. Fragments of it also turn up wherever an original god died, which is why a god's corpse counts as Primordial ground.

## Regions
- **The Progenitor Remains:** the bodies of beings like [[Ignis]], [[Gnome]], [[Undine]], and [[Sylph]]. They're closer to residue than living presences, but still the purest source of their Laws.
- **The Cage of [[Iron]]:** where Iron is trapped, still alive and not yet a Law. Nobody knows what keeps him there.
- **God-falls:** the places where original gods died. Their remains leave a Primordial scar in whatever realm it happened.

## Inhabitants
Almost nothing lives here. Remains, echoes of the progenitors, and the occasional god or 1st Finger searching for a Primary piece (see [[Class]]).

## Getting there
Through the depths of the Spirit Realm, or by standing where an original god died. Either way, it's a campaign goal, not a trip.

## Materials (Primordial 1–10)
Law-ash (3), progenitor bone (7), heart shard of an original god (10). Any Primordial material that comes from a progenitor also counts as a **Primary** acquisition toward that progenitor's class.

## Dangers
The remains still exert their Laws. Standing near Ignis's remains means burning. Mortals who take a piece often become the next target of every god who wants it.

The Spirit Realm is where the progenitor spirits — [[Ignis]], [[Gnome]], [[Undine]], [[Sylph]], and the rest of the entities the Laws were pulled from — exist apart from the mortal world. Most progenitors are already dead; their corpses became the Laws mortals now draw on, and what's left of them in the Spirit Realm is closer to residue than a living presence.

Not every progenitor died, though. [[Iron]] is the clearest known exception — still trapped in the Spirit Realm rather than dead, which is why Iron's power behaves differently from its siblings' and why no confirmed [[Class]] has been built around it yet. What keeps a progenitor alive there instead of letting it die into its Law is not understood, even by those who study the Laws closely.

The Spirit Realm isn't accessible to mortals under ordinary circumstances. What little interacts with it does so indirectly — through the diluted Laws themselves, or through the [[Shaman]] and [[Elves]] bloodlines, who are said to sit closer to it than most mortals ever will.

Sylph is the spirit of Air, one of the progenitors who lived in the [[Spirit Realm]] before her corpse became the [[Air]] Law. The old records call her the only progenitor that never stayed in one place long enough to be drawn: a voice, a pressure, a direction the grass bent.

Sylph left more children than any other progenitor: the four winds [[Boreas]], [[Zephyrus]], [[Notus]], and [[Eurus]], and [[Vortex]], which may be less a child than the shape of her dying. Her children took her death harder than any other progenitor's heirs. Boreas still holds enough power to challenge a god, and Eurus went as far as [[Infinatas]] trying to bring her back.

Those of the spiritual bloodline, [[Shaman]] and [[Elves]] chief among them, draw more readily on what's left of Sylph than most. What remains of her lies in the [[Primordial Realm]] as a wind that never stops.

Like every other [[Class]], power tied to Sylph directly requires something bound to the spirit itself.
- **Primary:** a piece of Sylph's own remains, such as [[FAND/Atrious/Materials/Sylph Breath|Sylph Breath]]. Its unique ability lets the wielder become weightless at will, drifting on any wind.
- **Secondary:** a relic tied to one of her children. Its unique ability depends on the child: Boreas gives cold, Zephyrus gentleness and speed, Notus storms, Eurus renewal, and Vortex pull.
- **Tertiary:** anything touched by Sylph at one remove: a feather from a high peak, a bell rung only by wind. Raises power only.

Undine is the spirit of Water, one of the progenitors dwelling in the [[Spirit Realm]] before its corpse became the [[Water]] Law. Depicted in what little survives of the old records as formless and restless — never the same shape twice, always moving even when nothing around it did.

Undine's death produced two known children: [[Ice]] and [[Frost]], both stiller and more fixed than their parent ever was, as though something about dying settled Undine's restlessness into them permanently.

Those of the spiritual bloodline — [[Shaman]] and [[Elves]] chief among them — draw more readily on what's left of Undine than most, the same way they do with every progenitor spirit.

**D&D class:** [[FAND/Atrious/Classes/Sorcerer|Sorcerer]], [[FAND/Atrious/Subclasses/Undine Bloodline|Undine Bloodline]].

Like every other [[Class]], acquiring power tied to Undine directly (rather than the diluted Water Law, or Ice/Frost once removed) requires something genuinely bound to the spirit itself.
- **Primary** — a piece of Undine's own remains. Its unique ability lets the wielder's body flow like water for a few seconds at will — enough to slip through a gap no solid body could fit, or shrug off a blow that should have connected.
- **Secondary** — a relic tied to [[Ice]] or [[Frost]] rather than Undine directly. Its unique ability keeps the wielder's blood from ever fully freezing or overheating, steady regardless of the surrounding cold or heat.
- **Tertiary** — anything else touched by Undine at one remove: river ice, morning frost, still water. Raises power only.
